title: Output capacitance on MPM3833C rails exceeds the datasheet's 100 uF maximum, clearly so on VCCINT (186 uF).
what: The MPM3833C datasheet lists 10 uF minimum, 22 uF typical and 100 uF maximum output capacitance, measured at one test point (1.2 V out, 2 A) on engineering samples. The module uses constant-on-time control (each switching pulse lasts a fixed time), and too much output capacitance can make its load-step response unstable. U2 on VCCINT has 186 uF fitted, still about 140-150 uF after the capacitors lose value under DC voltage, and also has a 22 pF feed-forward capacitor (C3, output to FB) that the MPS circuit does not show. VCCAUX (144 uF nominal) is borderline after derating, while VCCO and VIN_3V3 are probably below 100 uF effective; MPS does not show that any of these combinations is stable.
where: Frontend. U2 (VCCINT_1V0): C4 100u, C10 47u, C2 22u, C5/C6/C90 4.7u, C7/C8/C9/C11/C91/C92/C93 0.47u, CFF C3 22 pF; C89 100u is DNP. U3 (VCCAUX_1V8): C15/C59 47u, C13 22u, C16/C17/C94/C95/C96 4.7u, small parts, CFF C14. U4 (VCCO_1V5): C42 47u, C22 22u, 8 x 4.7u, 11 x 0.47u, CFF C23. U16 (VIN_3V3, no CFF): Frontend capacitors, SWITCHED_3V3 behind U10, and the FPGA-LDO board's /VIN_3V3 through J2 pins 68-70.
evidence: Fitted capacitors to GND summed from exports/frontend/netlist.xml with DNP flags from Artix_Frontend_8L_V3.kicad_sch: VCCINT_1V0 186.4 uF; VCCAUX_1V8 143.6 uF; VCCO_1V5 113.0 uF (11 x 0.47 uF, not 12); VIN_3V3 164.1 uF on the Frontend (mostly 6.3 V 0603 22 uF parts), plus 44.1 uF on SWITCHED_3V3 (C104, C76) when U10 is on, plus 60.8 uF on exports/ldo_a /VIN_3V3; 1V4_GTP_IN 31.4 uF (within limit). 88 uF of the VIN_3V3 total is the required 22 uF input capacitors of U2, U3, U4 and U13 (C1, C12, C21, C85). The JLC BOM fits C4 (GRM21BR60J107ME15L, C141660). C15, C59 and C42 are Yageo CC0805MKX5R5BB476. Effective values after DC-bias derating are estimates; the schematic Effective_capacitance fields say pending except C5/C6. An MPS forum reply (thread 1886) warns of instability above 100 uF, and a user's 1.2 V simulation there went unstable on a 3 A step above about 180 uF of low-ESR ceramics.
source: MPS MPM3833C datasheet Rev 1.0 (12/3/2018): p5 Converter System table, COUT 10/22/100 uF at VIN 3.6 V, VOUT 1.2 V, IOUT 2 A (note 6, engineering-sample test); p14 COT control; pp15-16 output capacitor section; p17 Fig. 4 (no CFF). https://www.monolithicpower.com/en/documentview/productdocument/index/version/2/document_type/Datasheet/lang/en/sku/MPM3833CGRH-Z/document_id/4426/
consequence: VCCINT, and possibly VCCAUX, may ring or oscillate on load steps once the FPGA design runs. Start-up is not at risk (1.3 ms soft-start needs well under 1 A to charge these values).
suggested_action: Ask MPS to confirm U2 and U3 with these COUT values and the 22 pF CFF, or mark C4 not fitted so VCCINT drops below 100 uF; then do a load-step check on the first boards.
already_known: Partly: schematic V46 note on the VCCINT bypass group (V42: 'fitted total still exceeds the MPS limit') and the C89 Qualification field in Artix_Frontend_8L_V3.kicad_sch cover VCCINT only; no record lists it as an open item or covers VCCAUX, VCCO or VIN_3V3. Both reviewers rate it major, not a note.

title: High-case stack load at the 5 V pin comes within about 0.02-0.10 A of the 0.63 A minimum port current limit.
what: All Frontend and FPGA-LDO power enters on one HDMI contact, J3.19, and passes through U16. Each HDMI port on the HDMI Extension Board has a TPS2553 switch that holds current constant at its limit; U16 is a buck converter, so if its input sags it draws more current, which can brown out or cycle the stack. Built up from the project's per-rail estimate, the load is comfortably below the limit in the expected case but close to it in the high case with all stimulators on, and the LDO board's +/-12 V start-up surge will briefly hit the limit at every power-up. No Vivado power figure or measurement exists, so the files cannot settle this; a measurement on the first Frontend + FPGA-LDO stack can.
where: Frontend J3.19 VIN_5V (TP14) -> U16 -> VIN_3V3, which also leaves on J2 pins 68-70 to the FPGA-LDO board; HDMI Extension Board TPS2553 port switches U701-U708 with ILIM resistors R711-R718 = 37.4k.
evidence: The 'about 0.55 A' in U16's Rated_output_current field (exports/frontend/parts.csv) is the old whole-system allowance at 3.3 V (about 0.43 A at 5 V; overnight hand-off C17, routing hand-off line 85), so adding the LDO board's 155-215 mA to it counts that board twice. Rebuilt from inputs/hdmi/power_estimate/START_HERE.md Frontend-only rows (0.23 A expected, 0.42 A high at 3.3 V) plus the LDO board's 155-215 mA (parts review V21), with 3.315 V / (0.88 x 4.8 V) = 0.785 A at 5 V per A at 3.3 V: about 0.30-0.35 A expected and 0.48-0.50 A high at the 5 V pin. Full stimulation (8 x 128 x 22.5 uA = 23 mA, about 15 mA above the 8 mA already budgeted) adds about 0.05-0.11 A, giving 0.53-0.61 A high. LDO board start-up inrush: 0.5-1 A at 3.3 V for 1-2 ms. Port limit at 37.4k: 637 / 696 / 764 mA min / nom / max, about 630-771 mA with the 1% resistor. The 88% efficiency is assumed, not read from the curves. The J3 contact rating (0.8 A, Molex catalog) was not verified; another source gives 0.3 A (separate finding).
source: TI TPS2553 SLVS841G, eq. 1-3 (pp16-17) and section 8.5.1 (equations as read by other reviewers; the TI PDF text could not be decoded in this check); MPM3833C Rev 1.0 efficiency curves (not re-read); engineering judgement.
consequence: In the high case, ports may enter current limit and the stack may brown out or fail to start. The limit cannot simply be raised, because its maximum is already near the J3 contact rating, so a fix could mean a cable, board or power-architecture change.
suggested_action: Get a Vivado report_power or XPE figure and measure the first Frontend + FPGA-LDO stack at TP14, including start-up with the +/-12 V converter, before fixing R711-R718 and ordering eight stacks.
verification: Upheld after a third independent check
already_known: inputs/hdmi/power_estimate/START_HERE.md (gate A2: frontend power from Vivado). Reviewer agrees it is open; the Frontend's own 0.55 A figure makes it tighter than that record's 'expected' case.

title: The JLC BOM fits the commercial 0-85 C FPGA, and no thermal estimate shows the Frontend stays below 85 C.
what: The JLC BOM places JLC part C1521720, which the project record identifies as the commercial XC7A35T-2CSG325C (junction limit 85 C); the schematic names the industrial -2CSG325I (100 C). The 22.59 x 25.42 mm Frontend dissipates about 0.9 W at the expected load and about 1.6 W in the high case, and its bottom face sits 1.5 mm above the FPGA-LDO board. Simple still-air screens give a rise of roughly 35-55 K at expected load and up to about 85 K in the high case for the board on its own; heat shared with the stack lowers this and the close facing board raises it. The junction could pass 85 C in the high case or in a warm head-worn environment; the files cannot settle this, and an XPE figure plus a thermocouple test on a heated stack would.
where: Frontend U1 (top, 116.22, 113.0); regulators U2/U3/U4/U13 near the west edge and U16 at the north-east corner (122.74, 98.55); the whole Option A head stack.
evidence: Outline 22.59 x 25.42 mm, 574 mm2 per side (exports/frontend/board_stats.txt); 70% of bottom area occupied. DF40C mated height 1.5 mm (inputs/ldo_a/stack_fit_test_V10). Expected on-board power from inputs/hdmi/power_estimate/START_HERE.md: VCCINT 0.20 W, VCCAUX 0.108 W, VCCO 0.075 W, GTP 0.168 W, SWITCHED_3V3 0.099 W, plus buck and U16 losses, about 0.9 W. High case about 1.6 W: the finding's 2.1 W counted the 3.3 V that leaves on J2 pins 68-70 (up to about 1 W) as Frontend heat. Thermal screen with convection plus radiation (about 15-25 W/m2K per face): about 35-58 K/W with both faces free, about double with one face blocked; Option A stack envelope 9-12 K/W. JLC BOM line 41: U1 C1521720 (C grade; C1521749 is the I grade per V3_review/parts_status.csv). U16 Qualification field: thermal pending.
source: AMD DS181 v1.27.1 Table 2 (Tj 0-85 C commercial, -40-100 C industrial). AMD's page returned 404, so these ranges come from the project record and mirrored DS181 copies and are not checked against the current AMD PDF. Thermal estimate: engineering judgement.
consequence: A commercial-grade U1 may run past its rated junction temperature in the high case, with timing and leakage drift. Surface temperature of a head-worn stack of about 1.35 W is a separate open limit.
suggested_action: Decide record decision 2 before ordering: fit the I-grade part the schematic names, or get an XPE figure and run a heated-stack test with a thermocouple on U1 first.
already_known: inputs/frontend/V3_record/START_HERE.md decision 2 (U1 grade C vs I). Thermal is not discussed there.

title: Three fitted 0805 capacitors under the Frontend leave 0.05 mm worst-case clearance to the FPGA-LDO board.
what: The DF40C connector pair sets a 1.5 mm gap between the Frontend bottom and the FPGA-LDO top. Three fitted 0805 bulk capacitors on the Frontend bottom are 1.25 +/- 0.2 mm thick, which leaves 0.25 mm at nominal and 0.05 mm at maximum thickness, before solder mask on the LDO board and connector seating tolerance (Hirose gives none). Contact loss on the connector is unlikely, because the DF40 still engages with 0.45 mm of mating length; the real risk is a capacitor that carries the mating force and cracks. The files cannot settle the true gap; a measurement on the first assembled pair can.
where: Frontend bottom: C4 (GRM21BR60J107ME15L, 100 uF, VCCINT) at (122.80, 101.08); C42 and C59 (CC0805MKX5R5BB476, 47 uF) at (104.16, 97.725) and (107.03, 98.45). C89 at (122.80, 103.04) is DNP. Same geometry on Option A and Option B; under the capacitors the LDO board has L1 tracks and 0.26-0.35 mm vias but no parts.
evidence: Sides, positions and DNP flags from exports/frontend/parts.csv; JLC BOM and CPL in inputs/frontend/V3_order list C4, C42 and C59 and not C89 (JLC_ORDER_NOTES.txt line 17). Thickness 1.25 +/- 0.20 mm from the Murata GRM21BR60J107ME15 sheet p1 and the Yageo X5R specification V.30 (thickness class EB). Mate transform (213.5 - x, 239.57 - y) for Option A and (213.5 - x, 245.38 - y) for Option B places no LDO component under these capacitors; Option B's R4 and R19 are elsewhere. Solder mask over the LDO L1 features takes about 0.02 mm more. The fit test V10 used the 8L V1 placement; this was recomputed for V3. The record's proposed 0.95 mm maximum part (GRM219R60J476ME44D) is not applied (schematic V45 and V46 records).
source: Hirose DF40 catalog (1 Jun 2024 copy), p1 (1.5 mm stacking height, 0.45 mm effective mating length) and p8, https://www.hirose.com/en/product/series/DF40 ; Murata GRM21BR60J107ME15 reference sheet p1; Yageo Class 2 X5R product specification V.30 (6 Dec 2022) pp3, 6.
consequence: A capacitor at the top of its tolerance can be loaded by mating force or board flex and crack; a cracked C4 can short VCCINT.
suggested_action: Decide before ordering whether to apply the record's low-profile swap (0.95 mm maximum) at these positions; measure the mated gap on the first assembled pair.
verification: Upheld after a third independent check
already_known: inputs/ldo_a/stack_fit_test_V10/START_HERE.md (0.05 mm clearance). The FE-LDO mate review in this round also rates it major. Reviewer agrees with major.

title: Boot flash U7 (W25Q128JWYIQ) has no JLC stock and is a special-order package at Winbond.
what: U7 is the 21-ball wafer-level package (WLCSP, package code Y) of the W25Q128JW. Winbond marks it, and several other packages, as special order, with no lead time or minimum quantity given. JLC showed 0 in stock and -2 orderable on 11 Nov, so it is one of the five Frontend lines JLC cannot supply. The FPGA mode pins select boot from this flash, so without U7 each board must be configured over JTAG, and fitting a bottom-side 0.5 mm-pitch WLCSP by hand afterwards is hard rework.
where: Frontend U7 W25Q128JWYIQ, bottom side (117.75, 104.5), JLC C6750401. U1 mode pins M2/M1/M0 = GND/GND/VCCAUX_1V8 (Master SPI). JTAG on J3 pins 2/15/17/18.
evidence: inputs/frontend/V3_review/parts_status.csv row 44 and parts_lookup.json: C6750401 stock 0, orderable -2, minimum buy 3, read 2026-11-11 08:57-08:58; alternate C18185308 also 0 stock, minimum 441. Five boards need five parts. JLC_ORDER_NOTES.txt line 23 lists U7 among the five out-of-stock parts. U7's schematic Package_selection field in exports/frontend/parts.csv already says special order; the V3 record decision list does not. Live LCSC stock could not be read (loaded dynamically). W25Q128JWYIM (C6326898) uses the same package but has a different default QE setting and a separate datasheet; it is not verified as a substitute.
source: Winbond W25Q128JW datasheet Rev G (29 Jul 2021), section 11.1, printed p76 (YIQ marked note 1) and p77 (note 1: special order); section 10.7 p73 (Y package). https://www.winbond.com/resource-files/W25Q128JW_RevG_07292021%20Plus.pdf
consequence: Five assembled boards arrive without a boot flash, or the order waits on an unknown lead time.
suggested_action: Before the PCBA order, get a quoted lead time and minimum quantity from Winbond or a distributor, or consign parts to JLC.
already_known: Out-of-stock status is in V3_record/START_HERE.md decision 3 and independent REPORT.md finding 1. The special-order status is not recorded. Reviewers agree it blocks complete assembly.

title: Three out-of-stock parts are feedback resistors; building without them drives GTP rails above absolute max.
what: R7, R10 and R13 have no JLC stock and are the upper feedback resistors (output to FB pin) of U4, U5 and U6. If the order is built with these lines not placed, each lower resistor holds FB at 0 V and the regulator drives its output toward its input. MGTAVCC and MGTAVTT, the FPGA transceiver supplies, would then rise to about 1.35-1.4 V, above their 1.10 V and 1.32 V absolute maximums. VCCO_1V5 would rise to about 3.3 V; that is within the bank's 3.6 V absolute maximum, but it puts 3.3 V levels on 1.5 V lines to the ASIC boards, and U4's power-good stays low, holding U6 off and the FPGA in reset.
where: Frontend: R7 (VCCO_1V5 to Net-(U4-FB), U4 = MPM3833C, IN = VIN_3V3), R10 (MGTAVCC_1V0 to Net-(U5-FB)), R13 (MGTAVTT_1V2 to Net-(U6-FB)); U5/U6 = TPS74801, IN = 1V4_GTP_IN. Lower resistors R8, R11, R14. Also out of stock: R27 (1k pull-up from VCCAUX_1V8 to CABLE_TARGET_SENSE, J3 pin 1; not part of the boot flash) and U7 (boot flash).
evidence: inputs/frontend/V3_review/parts_lookup.json and parts_status.csv: R7 C2075271 orderable 0 (by_code C2073422 also 0), R10 C2087906 0, R13 C1870640 0, R27 C490807 -1160, U7 C6750401 -2 (minimum buy 3). Nets from exports/frontend/pads.csv. Setpoints: U4 0.6 x (1 + 150/100) = 1.5 V; U5 0.8 x (1 + 1.3/4.99) = 1.008 V; U6 0.8 x (1 + 2.49/4.99) = 1.199 V; U13 0.6 x (1 + 200/150) = 1.4 V on 1V4_GTP_IN. TPS74801 has no overvoltage protection and 50-165 mV dropout at 1.5 A in bias mode; MPM3833C supports 100% duty in dropout. 20 U1 VCCO pins are on VCCO_1V5 and 109 nets join U1 to J1/J2. U4 PG drives BOOT_RAILS_PG_3V3 (U12 MR, U6 EN). The JLC_ORDER_NOTES.txt remark says only 'to be sourced or consigned'; JLC does not drop out-of-stock lines without the customer choosing to.
source: AMD DS181 v1.27.1 (3 Jul 2024) Table 1 (MGTAVCC 1.1 V, MGTAVTT 1.32 V, HR VCCO 3.6 V absolute maximum) and Table 2 (0.97-1.03 V, 1.17-1.23 V), https://docs.amd.com/api/khub/documents/iAkxxTOk96ANLJqYf2hgrQ/content ; TI TPS74801 datasheet (VREF 0.8 V, dropout), https://www.ti.com/product/TPS74801 ; MPS MPM3833C Rev 1.0 (VFB 0.6 V, 100% duty, protections).
consequence: Boards built without R10 or R13 would put above-maximum voltage on the GTP supplies at first power-up, likely damaging U1. Without R7 the board holds itself in reset with wrong I/O levels; without U7 it cannot boot from flash.
suggested_action: Secure R7, R10 and R13 before ordering (Global Sourcing, consignment or an in-stock equivalent of the same value and tolerance), and add to the assembly remark that the board must not be built with any of them missing.
already_known: START_HERE.md (V3 record) decision 3 lists the five parts as out of stock, but does not say that three are feedback resistors. Reviewer agrees they must be resolved before ordering.

title: No panel is drawn, and the order remark sends break-off tabs to the east edge, 0.665 mm from J1's pads.
what: JLC's Standard PCBA (assembly) service needs a board or panel of at least 70 x 70 mm with edge rails and fiducials (optical alignment marks). The Frontend is 22.59 x 25.42 mm, has no fiducials, and no panel is drawn; the PCB remark leaves the panel to JLC and asks for break-off tabs ('mouse bites', small perforated bridges snapped after assembly) on the south and east edges only. Along most of the east edge the 70-pin, 0.4 mm-pitch DF40 connector J1 sits 0.665 mm from the edge, and along the south edge small capacitors, a resistor and bare test pads sit 0.50 to 0.66 mm in. The project record judged the east edge free at a 0.6 mm keep-off, which ignores the clearance a tab needs.
where: Frontend outline x 102.21-124.80, y 96.50-121.92 mm. East edge: J1 (bottom, DF40C-70DS) pads x 120.355-124.135 over y 105.67-119.47, courtyard to x 124.68 (0.12 mm from the edge). West edge: J2 pads 0.645 mm in. South edge: test pads TP1/6/7/8/9/10/11/13 0.50 mm, C45/C49 (0402 4.7 uF, bottom) 0.52 mm, R9 (0201 resistor, top) 0.66 mm.
evidence: exports/frontend/board.json pad boxes with a 1.0 mm keep-off: the east edge is clear only at y 103.77-105.67 (1.9 mm) and y 119.47-121.92 (2.45 mm); the south edge has clear stretches of 3.54, 2.62, 1.95 and 4.58 mm, the two widest next to the ends of J2 and J1, whose courtyards are 0.975 mm from the south edge. With pcbnew courtyards (boards/frontend/Artix_Frontend_8L_V3.kicad_pcb) no edge has a 1.0 mm clear stretch; the best is 0.98 mm at the east edge, y 120.94-121.92. parts.csv has no fiducial footprints. inputs/frontend/V3_order/JLC_ORDER_NOTES.txt asks for tabs 'on the south and east edges only' and for JLC to add rails, fiducials and tooling holes. JLC_CHECKLIST.csv rows 34-37 call the east edge free at 0.6 mm keep-off (margin 0.065 mm).
source: JLCPCB PCB Assembly Capabilities (Standard PCBA: 70 x 70 mm minimum board or panel; edge rails and fiducials necessary), https://jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-assembly-capabilities; JLCPCB HDI PCB page (minimum V-cut panel 30 x 60 mm; smaller panels need tab-routing or stamp-hole panelization), https://jlcpcb.com/pcb-fabrication/hdi-pcb; JLC blog panelization guidance (1.5 to 5 mm component-to-tab clearance, figures vary between posts). Tab stress on J1 joints and the stack-fit effect of leftover nubs is engineering judgement.
consequence: JLC can probably add rails and tabs itself, but at a place of its choosing, and the remark currently points it at the east edge beside J1. Snapping a tab there can crack J1 solder joints or the small south-edge parts, and leftover nubs sit on edges that set the stack fit.
suggested_action: Before ordering, draw the panel (rails, fiducials, tooling holes) with tabs only in the clear south stretches and east-edge corners, or ask JLC to route the boards out fully; either way remove 'east' from the tab instruction.
already_known: START_HERE.md decision 1; JLC_CHECKLIST.csv 'Room for break-off tabs' (Ask JLC). The record calls the east edge free at 0.6 mm keep-off, but J1's joints are 0.665 mm in. Reviewer agrees it is a pre-order decision.

title: If a design drives FPGA ball M15 (EN_GTPWR) low, the FPGA resets itself and can reboot in a loop.
what: FPGA ball M15 turns on the 1.4 V transceiver (GT) supply U13; U13's power-good starts regulator U5 (MGTAVCC), and U5's power-good is on the same net that drives the reset supervisor U12's manual-reset input. U12 then pulls PROGRAM_B and INIT_B low, which erases the FPGA configuration. So a design that drives M15 low erases itself; M15 then floats, R58 turns GT power back on, U12 releases about 1.07 s later and the same design reloads, so it can repeat. Holding configuration off while a GT rail is bad is intended and required (the GT calibration runs only during configuration), so the only defect is that M15 cannot be used to switch GT power at runtime; no record states that M15 must stay high.
where: Frontend: U1.M15 EN_GTPWR_1V5 (R58 4.99k to VCCO_1V5) -> U15 SN74AXC1T45 -> EN_GTPWR_3V3 (R57 10k to GND) -> U13.4 EN; U13.12 PG_GTP_1V4 -> U5.5 EN; U5.3 PG on BOOT_RAILS_PG_3V3 (with U4.12 PG, U6.5 EN, U12.3 MR, R9, TP10); U12.6 BOOT_RESET_N -> U11 (74AUP2G07) -> U11.6 FPGA_PROGRAM_B (U1.P10), U11.4 FPGA_INIT_B (U1.T10).
evidence: exports/frontend/netlist.xml: BOOT_RAILS_PG_3V3 = R9.2, TP10.1, U12.3 MR, U4.12 PG, U5.3 PG, U6.5 EN; EN_GTPWR_1V5 = R58.2, U1.M15, U15.3; EN_GTPWR_3V3 = R57.1, U13.4, U15.4; PG_GTP_1V4 = R43.2, U13.12, U5.5; BOOT_RESET_N = R47.2, U11.1/.3, U12.6, U14.2. U15 supplies (VCCO_1V5 from U4, SWITCHED_3V3 from U10) do not depend on BOOT_RAILS_PG, so the loop does not latch off. PUDC_B (U1.J18) is pulled high by R25 470R, so M15 floats during configuration. C84 = 1 uF on U12 CT gives 1.07 s/uF x 1 uF = about 1.07 s. XC7A35T bitstream 17,536,096 bits at the default 3 MHz CCLK = about 5.8 s, so about 7 s per cycle (no CONFIGRATE set). Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc lines 118-119 set only pin and LVCMOS15; the comment calls M15 an output. Schematic text: 'default-enable and shutdown function'.
source: AMD UG482 7 Series FPGAs GTP Transceivers User Guide v1.9 (19 Dec 2016), p.219 (RCAL runs only during configuration; analog supplies valid before configuration), https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/ug482_7Series_GTP_Transceivers; AMD UG470 7 Series FPGAs Configuration User Guide v1.17 (5 Dec 2023), p.21 Table 2-4 (PROGRAM_B, INIT_B), Table 1-1 (bitstream size), p.158 (PROGRAM_B does not reset the JTAG TAP), https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/ug470_7Series_Config; TI TPS3890 SLVSD65A, p3 pin functions (MR), p5 timing, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps3890.pdf; TI TPS74801 SBVS074N (Jun 2024), section 6.3.2 (PG asserts when disabled).
consequence: A gateware default of 0 on M15, or a firmware attempt to power-cycle the GT link, turns the board into a reboot loop that looks like a power or flash fault at bring-up. GT power gating, the stated purpose of M15, cannot be used without a full reconfiguration.
suggested_action: Write 'M15 must be driven high or left undriven' into the XDC and the schematic note, and check that Vivado's default unused-pin pulldown (from memory, not verified) cannot pull M15 below U15's input threshold through R58 4.99k.

title: No record sets the GTP cable line rate, and the only stated figure, 1.25 Gb/s, cannot carry eight ASICs.
what: Each Frontend sends the data of eight ASICs over one transceiver (GTP) lane in the HDMI cable: 1.536 Gb/s of payload with packed 12-bit samples, or 2.048 Gb/s with 16-bit words. After line coding (8b/10b adds 25 %, 64B/66B about 3 %) and with the 125 MHz reference, that needs 2.0 Gb/s (64B/66B), 2.5 Gb/s (8b/10b, packed 12-bit) or 3.125 Gb/s (8b/10b, 16-bit words, which the weekly deck's 2 GB/s for 64 ASICs implies). The only records that state a rate, the HDMI design inputs and the power estimate, assume about 1.25 Gb/s because they counted one ASIC per port. The hardware supports every candidate rate and the HDMI board's recording-lane routing does not depend on the 1.25 Gb/s figure, so what is open is the rate decision and a cable loss check at that rate.
where: Frontend U1 (XC7A35T-2CSG325I) GTP TX0 H1/H2 -> J3.3/J3.5 -> about 1.8 m Micro-HDMI cable -> HDMI Extension Board J610-J617 pins 3/5 -> U801 ESD, C745-C760 AC capacitors -> MC3 GTY receivers. Reference: Y1 125 MHz LVDS on GTP REFCLK1 (B5/B6).
evidence: Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc: 64 unique ASIC1..8_DATA1..8 nets. ASIC_REFERENCE.md line 51: 256 Mb/s raw, 192 Mb/s payload per ASIC. 8 x 192 = 1.536 Gb/s (/0.8 = 1.92 Gb/s; x66/64 = 1.584 Gb/s); 8 x 256 = 2.048 Gb/s (/0.8 = 2.56 Gb/s). GTP PLL at 125 MHz gives 1.875, 2.0, 2.5 or 3.125 Gb/s at divider 2 (divider sets from memory of UG482). inputs/hdmi/design_inputs/START_HERE.md line 17: 'about 1.25 Gb/s (assumed)' from 256 Mb/s per port; inputs/hdmi/power_estimate/START_HERE.md line 31 repeats 1.25 Gb/s; ROUTING_GROUND_RULES_V1.md line 34: line rate not issued. title: Most ASIC lanes that change layer at J2 have no ground via stack within 3 mm to carry their return current.
what: When a signal changes layer through a via, its return current must also move between the ground planes next to each layer; a ground via close by gives it a short path. At J2, 34 lanes on L8 and L10 drop to L14 through a buried via plus laser microvias, so their return must move from the inner ground planes (L7, L9, L11) to L13; the 24 L12 lanes keep L13 as one reference, so only about half their return has to move. The only full ground via stack in the J2 field is north of the pins, so most of these returns detour 3 to 7 mm and share that detour, which breaks the project's own rule G05. The lanes are 32 MHz LVCMOS15 with default slow slew, so the effect is extra noise and crosstalk rather than a likely failure.
where: Frontend, J2 field x 102.2-107.5 mm, y 104.4-121.9 mm. Worst lanes: /ASIC5_DATA4 (103.02, 117.4) L10->L14 6.84 mm; /ASIC5_DATA2 6.60 mm; BOARD3_SPI_CLK L8 6.49 mm; /ASIC3_CLK32MHz_Out L10 4.98 mm; /ASIC1_CLK32MHz_Out L8 4.52 mm; /ASIC5_CLK32MHz_Out L12 3.92 mm; STIM_CLK_SHARED L8 3.39 mm. J2 GND pins 14, 15, 27, 34, 41, 50, 66 each have one L13-L14 microvia only.
evidence: exports/frontend/board.json vias (scratch/frontend-layout/returns.py, re-run independently): J2 has 58 lane transitions, 55 over 2 mm and 48 over 3 mm from the nearest full GND stack; median 5.08 mm on L8 (13 lanes), 5.17 mm on L10 (21), 3.26 mm on L12 (24). J1 by the same measure: maximum 2.25 mm. All 55 GND buried vias are in full stacks (4-11 + 11-12 + 12-13); in the J2 field the only one is at (106.0, 104.4), next nearest (108.0, 112.4), (109.42, 114.2), (110.22, 116.6), (109.42, 119.8). Distance from J2 GND pins to the nearest stack: 1.81 to 6.35 mm. zones.csv: GND planes on L2, L7, L9, L11, L13; no GND on L12 or L14. XDC: J2 nets LVCMOS15, no SLEW or DRIVE. Estimated extra return inductance a few tenths of a nH per lane (textbook via-pair formula, L11-L13 cavity 0.172 mm).
source: Project routing ground rules V1, G05 (inputs/frontend/routing_rules/ROUTING_GROUND_RULES_V1.md, line 15): a signal via needs a nearby, connected ground-return transition. G05 gives no distance; the 1 to 1.5 mm target, and the J1 side showing about 1.2 mm is achievable, are engineering judgement.
consequence: Lanes, including returned 32 MHz clocks and SPI clocks, share a longer return path, adding ground bounce, crosstalk and radiated noise near the ASIC connector; with no ASIC edge-rate data, a glitch at bring-up cannot be ruled out. It is cheap to fix now and hard after the boards are built.
suggested_action: Before ordering, add full GND via stacks (L13 up through the buried via) beside the J2 GND pins and in the J2 via rows where room allows, then re-run the same return-distance check aiming for under 1 to 1.5 mm.
already_known: Partly: codex_overnight_review/CLAUDE_HANDOFF.md C06/C07 (3 Nov, older board) raised the same pattern. It is not listed as open in V3_record/START_HERE.md.

title: 407 stacked laser-via columns and 577 lasers on buried vias need JLC's written acceptance before ordering.
what: The U1, J1 and J2 escapes are built almost entirely from stacked vias: laser-drilled microvias placed directly on top of each other and directly on the capped L4-L11 buried vias. JLC's published HDI rules do cover stacked vias, define them as aligned blind and buried vias, and offer the 3rd-order process this needs. What JLC does not publish is a limit on stack height or any reliability test or coupon, and it says staggered (offset) vias are generally preferred for yield. The order remark says the lasers are stacked but gives no quantities, so JLC's engineering review, which happens before payment, has to confirm it.
where: Frontend, mainly the U1 BGA field (272 of 324 U1 balls have a via in the pad centre) and the J1/J2 fan-out. 226 three-high stacks on L1-L2-L3-L4 and 181 on L11-L12-L13-L14 (407 columns at 383 sites); 24 sites are full L1-L14 stacks. 261 of 384 buried vias carry a 3-4 laser on top and all 316 11-12 lasers sit under a buried via.
evidence: exports/frontend/board.json and vias.csv, 2,664 vias grouped by exact x/y (995 sites): vias per site 1:386, 2:177, 3:68, 4:171, 5:146, 6:23, 7:24; no site mixes nets. Span counts 1-2 525, 2-3 342, 3-4 315, 4-11 384 (0.15/0.30 mm), 11-12 316, 12-13 336, 13-14 446; lasers 0.10 mm hole / 0.25 mm land. drc.json holes_co_located 81 (60 buried + 11-12, 21 buried + 3-4), all same-net. JLC_ORDER_NOTES.txt: lasers 'stacked on each other and on the buried via', no counts. JLC_CHECKLIST.csv row 6 (HDI order 'Within'), row 9 (stack-up 'Ask JLC'). Template JLCH141611Y3-1078 is a 3-step stack.
source: JLCPCB HDI PCB Capabilities FAQ (stacked-via and skip-via definitions; blind vias filled and planarised, buried vias resin plugged and capped; 3rd order = three laminations and three laser drillings; no stack limit), https://jlcpcb.com/help/article/hdi-pcb-capabilities-faq, read 11 Nov 2026; JLCPCB HDI PCB page (stacked and staggered both supported, staggered generally preferred; testing named is optical inspection and four-wire resistance; engineering review before payment), https://jlcpcb.com/pcb-fabrication/hdi-pcb. Stacked-microvia reliability concern: engineering judgement; IPC-WP-023 not read.
consequence: JLC may re-quote, ask for changes or build with an unstated yield and stacked-microvia reliability; tall stacks can fail open after reflow cycles. A forced move to staggered vias would mean re-routing the U1 field, but that is unlikely given JLC's published support.
suggested_action: Add the stack counts to the PCB remark and get JLC's written acceptance of three-high stacks on capped buried vias and full L1-L14 stacks in its pre-payment engineering review, with the existing 'Ask JLC' stack-up row.
verification: Upheld after a third independent check
already_known: V3_record/START_HERE.md ('Ask JLC' rows: stack-up) and the .kicad_dru header, which lists stacked lasers and laser-on-buried as assumptions; the counts are not recorded. frontend-layout rates it major because the answer gates the order; frontend-order rated it minor.

title: The placement file uses KiCad's raw bottom angles; ten bottom parts at 0 or 180 degrees flip under 180-minus.
what: The placement (CPL) file gives JLC the position and rotation of every part. It copies KiCad's footprint angle for all 170 rows, including 124 on the bottom, which is the route JLC's own KiCad guide describes; JLC states no separate bottom-side rule. Some widely used tools (the kicad-jlcpcb-tools plugin, KiBot's JLC example) instead write 180 minus the angle for bottom parts, which turns parts at 0 or 180 degrees by half a turn and leaves parts at 90 or 270 unchanged. JLC applies its own per-part offsets and its engineers check polarity from the silkscreen, but U7, U12, Y1, J1 and J2 on the bottom have no usable pin-1 silk mark, so the preview check decides those.
where: Frontend bottom parts (CPL degrees): U5, U6, U8, U10, U14, U18, Y1, Y2 at 0; U15, U17 at 180 (these ten change under 180-minus); U7 270, U11 90, U12 90, J1 90, J2 90 (unchanged). No silk on U7, Y1, J1, J2; U12 keeps only one short body line near pin 1. J3 is on the top side and keyed by its shield slots.
evidence: inputs/frontend/V3_order/Artix_Frontend_8L_V3_14L_V3_CPL_JLC.csv: rotation equals exports/frontend/board.json footprint rotation on 170 of 170 rows (124 Bottom, 46 Top). inputs/frontend/V3_scripts/make_jlc.py writes Rot % 360 from KiCad's position export with no side handling. pcbnew silk items: U7, Y1, J1, J2 zero; U12 one line (114.4, 97.85 to 98.58; pad 1 at 114.0, 98.55). kicad-jlcpcb-tools fabrication.py uses (180 - rotation) % 360 for bottom parts. JLC_ORDER_NOTES.txt asks JLC to confirm placement, polarity and rotation; V3_record/START_HERE.md lines 61, 75 and 101 list the preview check and assembly PDFs with pin 1 in red.
source: JLCPCB 'How to generate the BOM and Centroid file from KiCad' (Method 1: KiCad .pos export with renamed columns; no bottom-side rule), https://jlcpcb.com/help/article/how-to-generate-the-bom-and-centroid-file-from-kicad; JLCPCB PCB Assembly FAQs (engineers correct rotation and polarity from silkscreen, e-mail when unmarked); kicad-jlcpcb-tools fabrication.py and KiBot position notes; engineering judgement.
consequence: If both JLC's review and the preview check miss it, a 180-degree error on a regulator, oscillator or connector puts power or signals on the wrong pins and can damage the board at power-up.
suggested_action: Before paying, check pin 1 of the ten 0/180-degree bottom parts and of U7, U12, Y1, J1 and J2 in JLC's placement preview against the assembly PDFs, and keep 'confirm placement' selected.
already_known: START_HERE.md 'Not done / not verified' says rotations were not compared with JLC's part pictures. Reviewer agrees and treats this as a hard gate before ordering.

title: The schematic names the industrial-grade FPGA, but the JLC order places the commercial grade from inventory.
what: The schematic and KiCad exports call for XC7A35T-2CSG325I, the industrial grade (die, or junction, temperature -40 to 100 C). The JLC order instead fits XC7A35T-2CSG325C, the commercial grade (0 to 85 C), on purpose: 100 of these are already held in the project's JLC parts inventory, and the order note tells JLC to use them. The two grades are electrically the same apart from temperature range, so pinout, timing, transceiver limits and bitstream do not change. What remains is that the built board will not match its schematic, the BOM Comment field carries both part numbers, and the commercial part has a 15 C lower junction ceiling that no Frontend thermal estimate exists to judge.
where: Frontend FPGA Board, U1; JLC BOM line 41 (C1521720 = -2CSG325C); alternative C1521749 (-2CSG325I).
evidence: Schematic V46 Value/MPN/Drawing_Value on every U1 unit, exports/frontend/bom.csv line 43, parts.csv line 168 and pos.csv line 166: XC7A35T-2CSG325I. inputs/frontend/V3_order/Artix_Frontend_8L_V3_14L_V3_BOM_JLC.csv line 41: Comment 'XC7A35T-2CSG325I XC7A35T-2CSG325C', LCSC C1521720. JLC_ORDER_NOTES.txt line 21: use the -2CSG325C (C1521720) from inventory, marked [CONFIRM]. inputs/system/parts_sourcing_V1/GROUP_MESSAGE.md and PARTS_STOCK_5_vs_10.csv line 41: 100 x -2CSG325C held, chosen for U1 on 5 Nov. V3_review/parts_status.csv row 41: C1521720 orderable 18, 67.71 USD; parts_lookup.json: C1521749 orderable 64, 86.02 USD; 5 needed. The JLC CPL has no part-number column. The XDC line 1 comment names only 'XC7A35T-CSG325'; an XDC file does not set the device part, and no Vivado project file is in the inputs. No Frontend thermal or power estimate was found in the inputs.
source: AMD DS181 Artix-7 FPGAs Data Sheet v1.27.1 (3 Jul 2024), p.1 (all DC/AC parameters equal per speed grade except temperature range) and Table 2 p.3 (Tj 0 to 85 C commercial, -40 to 100 C industrial), https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/ds181_Artix_7_Data_Sheet; schematic V46; V3_record/START_HERE.md decision 2.
consequence: Files and boards disagree, which confuses later debugging and reorders. The 85 C ceiling would only bind at a board temperature already unacceptable on an animal's head (engineering judgement, not a calculation).
suggested_action: Confirm the commercial grade and write XC7A35T-2CSG325C into the schematic value/MPN with a single part number in the JLC BOM Comment, or order C1521749 instead; record a Frontend thermal estimate as a separate item.
verification: Upheld after a third independent check
already_known: inputs/frontend/V3_record/START_HERE.md decision 2. frontend-fpga and frontend-parts agree it is a pre-order decision rated minor; frontend-order rates it major.

title: The pin constraints omit the configuration settings, GTP pin locations and TX polarity the board needs.
what: Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc places all 116 user ports but sets no CFGBVS, CONFIG_VOLTAGE, SPI_BUSWIDTH or CONFIGRATE, and does not place the one wired transceiver (GTP) or its reference clock. The board needs CFGBVS GND and CONFIG_VOLTAGE 1.8; without a CONFIGRATE the FPGA reads its flash at the default 3 MHz, so boot takes about 5.8 s. The flash read data passes through the U8 level translator twice and must arrive within the low part of the configuration clock (CCLK), which can be as short as 40 % of the period; with the +/-50 % CCLK tolerance this limits the nominal setting to about 13.2 MHz, so CONFIGRATE 12 is safe and 16 is not. The TX pair is swapped P/N at J3 on purpose (schematic V42 note), so the gateware must also set TXPOLARITY = 1, which no constraint or gateware file records.
where: Frontend FPGA Board: inputs/frontend/V2_review_fixes/Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc; U1 E12 CFGBVS_0 = GND, E10/R10 VCCO_0 = VCCAUX_1V8; U1.E8 CCLK -> U8 pin 1 -> pin 12 -> U7 SCK; U7 DO -> U8 B4 -> A4 -> U1.L17 D01_DIN; GTP TX0 H2/H1 -> J3.5/J3.3 (GTP_TX0_P/N); MGTREFCLK1 B6/B5 via C78/C79; MGTREFCLK0 D6/D5 unconnected.
evidence: XDC: 120 lines, 116 set_property PACKAGE_PIN lines, 0 hits for CFGBVS/CONFIG_VOLTAGE/BITSTREAM/CONFIGRATE/POLARITY; a comment line lists B5/B6 and H1/H2 as not constrained. exports/frontend/netlist.xml: E12 on GND, VCCO_0 on VCCAUX_1V8, mode pins M2/M1 = GND, M0 = 1V8 (Master SPI); D5/D6 'unconnected-(U1D-MGTREFCLK0...)'; GTP_TX0_N -> J3.3, GTP_TX0_P -> J3.5. exports/hdmi/netlist.xml: J610.3 = MGT_RXP0_224, J610.5 = MGT_RXN0_224. Read-path budget: U8 A->B 5.2 ns + flash tCLQV 6 ns + U8 B->A 6.0 ns + DIN setup 3.0 ns = 20.2 ns; 20.2 / 0.4 = 50.5 ns -> 19.8 MHz actual; 19.8 / 1.5 = 13.2 MHz nominal. Boot at default: 17,536,096 bits / 3 MHz = 5.8 s (11.7 s at -50 %). Vivado's CONFIGRATE steps (..., 12, 16, 22, ...) are from memory.
source: AMD UG470 7 Series FPGAs Configuration User Guide v1.17 (5 Dec 2023), Table 2-3 (CFGBVS) and bitstream length, https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/ug470_7Series_Config; AMD DS181 v1.27.1 pp.58-59 (FMCCK_START 3 MHz, FMCCKTOL +/-50 %, TMCCKL/TMCCKH 40/60 %, TSPIDCC 3.00 ns), https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/ds181_Artix_7_Data_Sheet; TI SN74AVC4T774 SCES693I (Feb 2025) p.9 table 5.7, VCCA 1.5 V / VCCB 1.8 V, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/sn74avc4t774.pdf; Winbond W25Q128JW Rev G (29 Jul 2021) p.64 tCLQV, https://www.winbond.com/resource-files/W25Q128JW_RevG_07292021%20Plus.pdf.
consequence: Vivado warns on CFGBVS/CONFIG_VOLTAGE and boot is slow; a later speed-up to 16 MHz or more can give intermittent corrupt flash reads. A GT placed on the wrong channel or reference clock, or left at normal polarity, gives a dead or inverted recording link on a correct board.
suggested_action: Before the first bitstream, add CFGBVS GND, CONFIG_VOLTAGE 1.8, BITSTREAM.CONFIG.SPI_BUSWIDTH 1, CONFIGRATE 12 (or lower), PACKAGE_PIN H2/H1 for GTP TX0 and B6/B5 for MGTREFCLK1, and set TXPOLARITY = 1 in the GT setup.
already_known: U7 and U8 part fields mention 'CONFIGRATE 3MHz initial' and the 5.2/6 ns bound, but no limit or XDC setting is recorded. inputs/frontend/V3_record/START_HERE.md says the pin constraints were not run in Vivado.

title: JTAG reaches the FPGA only through the HDMI cable, with no test pads and no ESD clamp at either cable end.
what: JTAG is the four-wire programming and debug port (TCK, TMS, TDI, TDO). On the Frontend these four lines run straight from the Micro-HDMI connector J3 to the FPGA, with no ESD clamp (a part that diverts static discharge), no series resistor and no test pad. The cable's LVDS pairs are clamped by U17/U18, yet two spare U18 channels are tied to GND, and the HDMI Extension Board has only 100 ohm resistors on these lines, so neither end clamps JTAG. The only way to program or probe a Frontend is through the cable, the HDMI board's U611 switch and its USB-JTAG.
where: Frontend FPGA Board: J3.17 FPGA_JTAG_TCK -> U1.F8, J3.2 TMS -> U1.R8, J3.15 TDI -> U1.T9, J3.18 TDO -> U1.T8; J3.1 CABLE_TARGET_SENSE -> R27 (1k to VCCAUX_1V8); U18 pins 4-7 (IO3/IO4) on GND. HDMI Extension Board: J610 pins 17/15/18/2 -> R640-R643 -> U611 (same on all ports).
evidence: exports/frontend/netlist.xml: each of FPGA_JTAG_TCK/TMS/TDI/TDO has exactly two nodes (J3 pin, U1 ball). TP1-TP14 sit only on rails, GND, BOOT_RAILS_PG, INIT_B and DONE. U18 pins 4/5/6/7 on GND; its field says unused IO3/IO4 are tied to GND. exports/hdmi/netlist.xml: HDMI1_JTAG_TCK/TDI/TDO/TMS = J610 pin + R640/R641/R643/R642 only, far ends to U611 NO4/NO6/NO5/NO3. TCK and TDO use cable pins 17/18 (the HDMI SCL/SDA wires, not a shielded pair); crosstalk between them is plausible but unproven, and the cable length is not in the files.
source: AMD UG470 7 Series FPGAs Configuration User Guide v1.17 (5 Dec 2023), Table 2-4 (TCK), https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/ug470_7Series_Config; TI TPD4E02B04 SLVSD85B, as used on the cable LVDS lines, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tpd4e02b04.pdf; Engineering judgement on ESD and bench access.
consequence: A discharge while plugging the cable lands directly on bank 0, which also holds the configuration pins, and relies only on the FPGA's on-chip protection. If the HDMI board or cable path has a fault, a new Frontend cannot be programmed or probed at all.
suggested_action: Decide whether to accept this. If not, add JTAG test pads (with GND and 1.8 V) and clamp J3 pins 2/15/17/18, using the two spare U18 channels for TCK and TMS plus a second low-capacitance array like U17.

title: It is not established that Vivado can program the W25Q128JW boot flash in x1 mode.
what: The FPGA loads its design from flash U7 at power-up, and the boot image has to be written into that flash first, normally by Vivado over JTAG. Vivado only drives flash parts on its configuration-memory list, and U7 is a 1.8 V W25Q128JW wired for single-bit (x1) mode only. The files and the AMD pages that could be read do not settle whether this part, or an accepted compatible entry, is on the Artix-7 list; the part record still says the programmer flow is pending. Opening the 'Add Configuration Memory Device' list in the installed Vivado, or the Artix-7 table in UG908, would settle it.
where: Frontend FPGA Board: U7 W25Q128JWYIQ; U1 J15 (D02) and J16 (D03) unconnected; U7 IO2/IO3 held high by R20/R21 (FLASH_WP_N_1V8, FLASH_HOLD_N_1V8).
evidence: exports/frontend/netlist.xml: unconnected-(U1A-L2P_T0_D02-PadJ15) and (L2N_T0_D03-PadJ16); FLASH_WP_N_1V8 = U7.3 + R20; FLASH_HOLD_N_1V8 = U7.7 + R21. U7 Flash_setup field: 'SPIx1,QE=1 fixed ... programmer flow pending'. AMD UG908 per-family device pages on docs.amd.com returned HTTP 404; no local Vivado install was available. Web search shows W25Q256JW listed for Artix UltraScale+ and Spartan-7 (search snippet only); no W25Q128JW entry for Artix-7 was found.
source: AMD UG908 Vivado Design Suite User Guide: Programming and Debugging, configuration memory support tables (not readable here); AMD AR 50991, https://adaptivesupport.amd.com/s/article/50991.
consequence: If the part is not supported and no compatible entry or third-party loader works, the flash cannot be written with the standard flow and the board must be loaded over JTAG at every power-up.
suggested_action: Before ordering, check the target Vivado's configuration-memory list for w25q128jw or a usable x1 alias and record the part name to select; source U7 together with that answer.
verification: Checked once; the files cannot settle it
already_known: Programming support is new; only the stock problem is in inputs/frontend/V3_record/START_HERE.md decision 3 (see the U7 availability finding).

title: The separate SYNC pair is undriven on HDMI ports 1, 2, 7 and 8, and the Frontend cannot tell its port.
what: Every Frontend is the same and always feeds cable pins 12/14 (CABLE_SYNC) into an LVDS receiver in the FPGA, with only a 100 ohm resistor across the pair and no bias resistors. The HDMI Extension Board drives these pins only on ports 3-6; on the other four ports they are left open. An LVDS receiver with 0 V between its inputs (below its 100 mV minimum) can output either level or toggle on noise. The cable carries no port number, so the gateware cannot decide on its own whether to use this pair or the SYNC folded into pins 9/11.
where: Frontend FPGA Board: J3.12/J3.14 /CABLE_SYNC_P/N -> U18 clamp -> R64 100R -> U1.B9/A9 (bank 15, LVDS_25, DIFF_TERM FALSE). HDMI Extension Board: J612-J615 pins 12/14 driven (B64_L16/L23/L22/L18); J610, J611, J616, J617 pins 12/14 unconnected.
evidence: exports/frontend/netlist.xml: /CABLE_SYNC_P = J3.12, R64.1, U1.B9, U18.1/10; /CABLE_SYNC_N = J3.14, R64.2, U1.A9, U18.2/9; R64 100R (parts.csv row 153); no bias resistors. XDC: B9/A9 LVDS_25 DIFF_TERM FALSE. exports/hdmi/netlist.xml: J612-J615 pins 12/14 on B64_L16P/N, L23P/N, L22P/N, L18P/N (MC1) with U811-U814 clamps; J610, J611, J616, J617 pins 12/14 'unconnected-(...-SYNC_P/N-Pad12/14)'. J3.1 only sources 1.8 V through R27. Schematic V46 note: 'port-number strap or firmware selection not defined'.
source: AMD DS181 Artix-7 FPGAs Data Sheet v1.27.1 (3 Jul 2024), Table 11 LVDS_25 VIDIFF min 100 mV, VICM 0.3-1.5 V, https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/ds181_Artix_7_Data_Sheet; AMD UG471 v1.10 p.92 (external termination); Engineering judgement.
consequence: A Frontend on port 1, 2, 7 or 8 whose gateware uses CABLE_SYNC sees random sync pulses. No harm is done if the gateware ignores this pair there.
suggested_action: Write the rule into the gateware spec (CABLE_SYNC valid only on ports 3-6, or folded SYNC on 9/11 everywhere, or a port number sent in the command stream), or add a small fail-safe bias on the Frontend side.
already_known: Schematic V46 note (V41 paragraph): 'port-number strap or firmware selection not defined'. frontend-io agrees with a note rating; frontend-fpga rated it minor.

title: The JLC BOM buys plain TPS74801DRCR, which may be the 2 % chip, leaving MGTAVCC under 1 mV below its limit.
what: The schematic specifies TPS74801DRCRM3, the newer chip with a 1 % reference. The JLC order uses the plain TPS74801DRCR, and TI says parts without the M3 suffix may be the older chip with a 2 % reference. U5 is set to 1.0084 V for MGTAVCC (the FPGA transceiver core supply), so with a +2 % older chip and resistor tolerance it can reach about 1.0299 V against the 1.03 V maximum, before any ripple. U6 (MGTAVTT) keeps only about 4-5 mV above its 1.17 V minimum in the same case.
where: Frontend FPGA Board: U5 (MGTAVCC_1V0, R10 1.3k / R11 4.99k), U6 (MGTAVTT_1V2, R13 2.49k / R14 4.99k); JLC BOM line 43, C105263.
evidence: Netlist: U5/U6 MPN TPS74801DRCRM3; U5 Output_nominal 1.0084 V, U6 1.1992 V; R10/R11/R13/R14 all 0.1 %, 25 ppm. inputs/frontend/V3_order/Artix_Frontend_8L_V3_14L_V3_BOM_JLC.csv line 43: 'TPS74801DRCRM3 TPS74801DRCR, U5,U6, ..., C105263'. U5: 0.8 x (1 + 1.3/4.99) = 1.0084 V; 1.00842 x 1.02 x 1.0013 = 1.0299 V. U6: 1.19920 x 0.98 x 0.9987 = 1.1737 V. With R10 = 1.27k: 1.0036 V nominal, 0.983-1.024 V with a 2 % chip.

title: VIN_5V from the cable reaches U16 with no clamp, and hot-plug overshoot against its 6.5 V limit is unmeasured.
what: The 5 V from the HDMI cable goes straight to the input and enable pins of U16, the buck module that feeds every other rail. The only parts on that net are two 22 uF capacitors, one 100 nF capacitor and a test point; there is no TVS diode or other clamp. Plugging a cable into a live port can make the voltage ring above 5 V for a moment, because the cable's inductance and the ceramic capacitors form a lightly damped circuit. The current-limit switch on the HDMI board side should help damp this, but nobody has measured it, so the files cannot settle whether the peak stays below U16's 6.5 V absolute maximum; a scope capture at the first plug-in would.
where: Frontend: J3.19 -> net VIN_5V -> U16 pins 13, 14 (IN) and pin 4 (EN); C206, C207 (22 uF / 10 V, 0805), C209 (100 nF, 0201), TP14. HDMI Extension Board side: net PORT1_5V, U701 (TPS2553DBVR) with C721 (1 uF) at J610.19.
evidence: exports/frontend/netlist.xml net VIN_5V: C206.1, C207.1, C209.1, J3.19, TP14.1, U16.4/13/14 only; parts.csv has no D* part on it. parts.csv: C206/C207 GRM21BR61A226ME44L, C209 GRM033R61A104KE15D. MPM3833C datasheet p3: every pin except SW -0.3 to +6.5 V absolute maximum; VIN 2.75-6 V recommended. Source voltage 5.02 V (U700, HDMI board), leaving 1.48 V (30 %) to 6.5 V. exports/hdmi/netlist.xml PORT1_5V: U701.6, C721 1 uF, J610.19, TP701. Schematic V46 U16 note marks hot-plug overshoot as unverified.
source: MPS MPM3833C datasheet Rev 1.0, p3, Absolute Maximum Ratings and Recommended Operating Conditions, https://www.monolithicpower.com (MPM3833C product page); engineering judgement for the hot-plug ringing.
consequence: If the plug-in ringing is under-damped, for example with a short, thick cable, the peak could pass 6.5 V and damage U16, which would take down every rail on the board.
suggested_action: On the first board, scope VIN_5V at TP14 while plugging the real cable into a live HDMI board port, using the shortest planned cable. If there is spare area, add a DNP TVS footprint on VIN_5V and fit it if the peak exceeds 6 V.
already_known: Schematic V46 U16 note ('Unverified: cable hot-plug overshoot vs 6.5 V abs max'). frontend-power agrees it is minor.

title: The GT pair is P/N swapped by design, and no constraint file records that the Frontend GTP must invert it.
what: The recording data travel on one differential pair, a P wire and an N wire. On the Frontend, cable pin 3 carries N and pin 5 carries P, while on all eight HDMI Extension Board ports pin 3 goes to the receiver's P input and pin 5 to N, so a straight cable delivers inverted data. This is intended: gateware must set TXPOLARITY = 1 on the Frontend transmitter and must not also invert on the XEM receiver. The requirement is written in the Frontend schematic note (V42), the HDMI V35 review and the HDMI V36 record, but not in the current Frontend constraint file or any of the three HDMI constraint files; an earlier Frontend draft constraint file had it.
where: Frontend J3.3 = GTP_TX0_N (U1 H1, MGTPTXN0_216), J3.5 = GTP_TX0_P (U1 H2, MGTPTXP0_216). HDMI Extension Board J610-J613 pin 3 = MGT_RXP0..3_224, pin 5 = MGT_RXN0..3_224; J614-J617 pin 3 = MGT_RXP0..3_226, pin 5 = MGT_RXN0..3_226.
evidence: exports/frontend/netlist.xml: GTP_TX0_N = J3.3 + U1.H1; GTP_TX0_P = J3.5 + U1.H2. exports/hdmi/netlist.xml: pin 3 = RXP and pin 5 = RXN on 8 of 8 ports. Case-insensitive search for 'polarity': 0 hits in inputs/frontend/V2_review_fixes/Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc, and 0 in inputs/hdmi/firmware_V34/fit_pins_V34.xdc, fit_pins_V34_sync.xdc and header_pins_V34.xdc. Frontend XDC line 120 lists GTP TX0 H1/H2 as unconstrained with no polarity comment. Requirement recorded in the Frontend schematic note, inputs/hdmi/V36_prefab_fixes/START_HERE.md line 72 and the V35 ALL_FINDINGS.md.
source: AMD UG482 7 Series FPGAs GTP Transceivers User Guide v1.9, chapter 3, TX Polarity Control, p.106 (as cited in the schematic note; not re-read for this review), https://docs.amd.com/api/khub/documents/Xk_zMbXsJj92suJ4_0Akkg/content
consequence: If gateware inverts on both ends or on neither, the link never locks and no recording data arrive. The requirement is easy to lose because it is not in any constraint file.
suggested_action: Add one comment line to Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc and to the HDMI fit_pins constraint file stating TXPOLARITY = 1 on the Frontend GTP and RXPOLARITY = 0 on the XEM, and note it in the gateware record.
already_known: inputs/hdmi/V35_prefab_review/ALL_FINDINGS.md (P/N inversion, rated no-PCB-change). Reviewer agrees with that severity; the comment it asked for is still missing from both XDC files.

title: Bottom decoupling caps reach ground only via L13, a median 1.6 mm (up to 3.9 mm) from a full ground stack.
what: Decoupling capacitors on the bottom under the FPGA have a good via from the supply pad up to the supply plane, but the ground pad has only a single microvia (a tiny laser-drilled via) down to L13. L13 reaches the other ground planes (L2, L7, L9, L11) only through 55 full ground stacks, so each capacitor's current must run sideways on L13 to the nearest stack. That longer path adds loop inductance, which makes the capacitor less effective at high frequency. The added inductance is modest, about 0.5-0.8 nH per capacitor, not a failure.
where: Frontend, bottom side, under U1. Worst: C55 (MGTAVTT, 470 nF) 3.86 mm; C54 and C56 (MGTAVTT) 3.20 mm; C52 (MGTAVCC) 2.96 mm; C18 (VCCAUX) 2.85 mm; C51 2.76 mm; C5 (VCCINT, 4.7 uF) 2.52 mm. Ground pad microvias L14-L13.
evidence: exports/frontend/board.json: every GND buried via (2-3, 3-4, 4-11, 11-12, 12-13) is one of the same 55 stacks joining L2 to L13; 239 GND vias 1-2 and 163 GND vias 13-14 (155 alone). zones.csv: GND pours on L2, L7, L9, L11, L13; none on L14. Of 66 bottom rail capacitors (oscillator, soft-start and timing nets excluded), 56 have their ground pad more than 1 mm from the nearest stack; median 1.61 mm. Each ground pad has 1 microvia (4 on 0805 bulk capacitors). With L4-L13 about 1.13 mm (stackup.txt) and via radius about 0.075 mm: 4e-7 x 1.13e-3 x ln(1.6/0.075) = 1.38 nH, against 0.86 nH with a ground via 0.5 mm away. A 470 nF capacitor's resonance moves from about 8-10 MHz to about 5-7 MHz.
source: AMD UG483 7 Series FPGAs PCB Design Guide, chapter 2 (capacitor placement and mounting inductance), https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/ug483_7Series_PCB ; AMD UG482 for GTP supply noise. Neither could be opened for this review (the AMD URL returned 404); the numbers are engineering judgement.
consequence: Supply noise in roughly the 5-50 MHz band is somewhat higher than the capacitor count suggests, most importantly on the GTP supplies, where noise turns into transmit jitter.
suggested_action: Give the ground pad of each GTP supply capacitor (C51-C56), and of the worst VCCINT and VCCAUX capacitors, its own nearby full ground stack, then re-check the distances.

title: Cable pairs are about 88-93 ohm instead of 100 ohm, and the JLC remark sets no impedance target.
what: The six cable-pair nets (clock, command and SYNC) are routed as 0.08 mm tracks with a 0.31 mm gap, which gives about 88-90 ohm on L8 and 92-93 ohm on L10 against the 100 ohm target for HDMI cable and LVDS pairs. JLC's track-width tolerance of +/-20 % moves this by about +/-7 ohm. The JLC remark only asks JLC to report the impedance of this geometry; it states no target, so JLC will apply no impedance control. A decision is needed before upload: an order for 'controlled 100 ohm' would put the as-drawn copper at the edge of JLC's +/-10 % window.
where: Frontend: /CABLE_CLK_P/N on L8 (25.25 / 25.64 mm), /CABLE_CMDSYNC_P/N on L10 (23.66 / 24.09 mm), /CABLE_SYNC_P/N on L8 (6.43 / 6.39 mm); /CABLE_SYNC_N also has 1.86 mm on L12. inputs/frontend/V3_order/JLC_ORDER_NOTES.txt, Impedance line.
evidence: exports/frontend/nets.csv and board.json: 64 tracks of 0.08 mm, all on these six nets; most of the length at 0.39 mm centre pitch (0.31 mm gap), CLK has 3.2 mm at 0.80 mm pitch. stackup.txt: L7-L8 core 0.10 mm (er 4.11), L8-L9 prepreg 0.097 mm (er 4.29), L9-L10 core 0.10 mm, L10-L11 prepreg 0.112 mm. Field solve (scratch/frontend-layout/fd2d.py): 88.3 ohm (L8), 91.6 ohm (L10); closed-form stripline check: 88.6 / 92.3 ohm; record inputs/frontend/V3_review/impedance.json: 89.7 / 92.7 ohm, 0.15 mm-core variant 97.4 / 101.1 ohm. Sensitivity about 450-500 ohm per mm of width, so +/-0.016 mm gives about +/-7 ohm. Reflection at 90 ohm into 100 ohm: about 5 %. The remark's Tracks line names L8 / L10 / L12; its Impedance line omits the L12 piece, which is a short uncoupled single trace.
source: JLCPCB HDI PCB page, impedance at 50 ohm and above held to +/-10 %, https://jlcpcb.com/pcb-fabrication/hdi-pcb ; JLCPCB PCB capabilities, track width +/-20 %, https://jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-capabilities ; 100 ohm differential target for HDMI cable and LVDS (TIA/EIA-644); project routing rule G07.
consequence: The roughly 5 % reflection is harmless at 125 MHz over about 25 mm if the receiver termination is right. The real risk is ordering 'controlled 100 ohm' on this copper, which JLC would treat as out of tolerance.
suggested_action: Decide before upload: state about 90 ohm (as built) as the target, leave impedance control off, or take the 0.15 mm-core stack-up variant. Do not order 'controlled 100 ohm' on this copper.
already_known: V3_record/START_HERE.md decision 4 (90/93 ohm). Both reviewers agree it is a decision, technically minor.

title: Slow-net hop tracks cut 0.29 mm slots in ground layers L2 and L13 that nine L12 lanes and three L1 nets cross.
what: A few slow nets were routed as short 'hop' tracks inside the L2 and L13 ground pours, which cuts narrow slots in those planes. A signal track's return current flows in the plane right beside it, so where an L12 lane crosses an L13 slot it loses one of its two reference planes for 0.24-0.50 mm, and where an L1 track crosses an L2 slot it briefly loses its only reference. The crossings are short and L11 is whole above every L12 crossing, so the effect is small. The 25 MHz clock CLK25_PL is the crossing worth moving, and the project record's open list omits it.
where: Frontend. L12 lanes over L13 slots: /ASIC5_DATA5 (108.63, 117.9) 0.50 mm; CHIP_RESET_SHARED (113.0, 107.5) 0.46; /STIM_CHIP1_SPI_DR (108.52, 111.3) 0.41; /ASIC5_DATA6 0.35; CLK25_PL (117.2, 116.1) 0.29; /ASIC5_DATA7 0.29; /ASIC5_DATA8 0.29; /ASIC5_READ 0.25; /ASIC5_CLK32MHz_Out (108.76, 117.7) 0.24. L1 tracks over L2 slots: FPGA_JTAG_TDI (115.82, 118.2) 0.24 mm; BOOT_RAILS_PG_3V3 0.21; Net-(U3-FB) 0.18. /ASIC5_DATA8 on L12 also loses L11 for 0.55 mm twice at y 119.0, under foreign buried-via lands.
evidence: Filled zones re-dumped with pcbnew and every L12 and L1 track centreline sampled every 0.01 mm against the L13, L11 and L2 fills, excluding each net's own via antipads (scratch/verify-frontend-batch2/fill.py, refchk.py; original scratch/frontend-layout/refcheck2.py -> refgaps2.json). Results match to within 0.01 mm. Slots are owned by hop tracks of BOOT_RAILS_PG_3V3, FPGA_QSPI_CCLK, FPGA_INIT_B, EN_GTPWR_1V5 and JTAG_TDO. exports/frontend/board.json: L2 has 38 hop segments, 17.62 mm; L13 has 37, 18.90 mm; all 0.09 mm wide with 0.10 mm pour clearance. inputs/frontend/V2_review_fixes/START_HERE.md line 44 lists the open item without CLK25_PL.
source: Project routing ground rules V1, G05 (routing_rules/ROUTING_GROUND_RULES_V1.md); engineering judgement.
consequence: Small local impedance bumps and some extra crosstalk on the crossing tracks; the 25 MHz clock is the one where an edge disturbance matters most.
suggested_action: Move the CLK25_PL crossing off the L13 slot, or move the hop under it to another layer; do the same for /ASIC5_CLK32MHz_Out if it is easy, and leave the rest.
already_known: V2_review_fixes/START_HERE.md 'Still open' (19 hops, 0.29 mm slots, the same lane list). Reviewer agrees with minor; that list omits CLK25_PL.

title: Layer L5 is referenced to the split L4 power layer, so JTAG TDI runs 10.9 mm over the MGTAVCC pour.
what: L5 is a signal layer whose nearest plane is L4, 0.112 mm above, and L4 is cut into several separate supply pours; L6, 0.10 mm below, is another signal layer. A track's return current flows in the nearest plane, so FPGA_JTAG_TDI, which runs 10.9 mm over the MGTAVCC_1V0 pour, pushes its edge currents into the GTP transceiver core supply. INIT_B and some enable and power-good nets cross five or six different pours. Separately, TDO on L5 lies right over INIT_B on L6 for about 11 mm, so the two couple broadside (face to face through the thin dielectric).
where: Frontend L5: FPGA_JTAG_TDI (10.9 mm over MGTAVCC_1V0, 6.0 mm over VCCAUX_1V8); FPGA_INIT_B over VCCAUX, MGTAVTT, MGTAVCC, VIN_3V3 and 1V4_GTP_IN; EN_GTPWR_3V3 and PG_GTP_1V4 similar. L5/L6 broadside: FPGA_JTAG_TDO over FPGA_INIT_B for about 11 mm; BOOT_RAILS_PG_3V3 over INIT_B for about 7.6 mm.
evidence: exports/frontend/board.json layer names: L4-Power, L5-Signal, L6-Signal, L7-GND. stackup.txt: dielectric 4 is 0.112 mm, dielectric 5 is a 0.10 mm core. L4 fill owner sampled every 0.02 mm under each L5 track (scratch/verify-frontend-batch2/l5.py): TDI MGTAVCC 10.90 mm, VCCAUX 6.00 mm, none 1.07 mm; TDO VCCAUX 21.75 mm, MGTAVCC 3.07 mm. L5/L6 parallel within 0.3 mm: TDO/INIT_B 11.36 mm (10.6 mm in the original check, 10.5 mm in the record; the difference is the counting window); BOOT_RAILS_PG_3V3/INIT_B 7.61 mm. inputs/frontend/V2_review_fixes/START_HERE.md line 49 lists TDO beside INIT but not the MGTAVCC reference.
source: Engineering judgement. AMD UG482 (MGTAVCC noise limits) was not re-read for this review.
consequence: A small amount of noise enters MGTAVCC whenever JTAG is active, which includes in-system debug such as an ILA while the transceivers run. A fast TDO edge can also couple onto INIT_B, a configuration status line.
suggested_action: Re-route TDI so it stays over VCCAUX or GND, or move it to L6 over the L7 ground, and separate TDO from INIT_B by at least one track pitch.
already_known: V2_review_fixes/START_HERE.md lists TDO beside INIT (10.5 mm). The MGTAVCC reference is not listed.

title: Four MPM3833C modules use 0603 input capacitors and have no added SW copper, against the maker's layout guide.
what: The MPM3833C buck module datasheet asks for an 0805 ceramic input capacitor as close to the pins as possible, wired directly to IN and PGND, and for extra copper on the SW (switch-node) pin to carry heat away. On U2, U3, U4 and U13 the input capacitors are 22 uF 0603 parts about 1.8 mm from the IN pin, and the SW pads have no copper beyond the pad itself. A smaller ceramic capacitor loses more of its capacitance under DC voltage (DC bias), so the 0603 parts give less effective capacitance at 3.3 V. The direct capacitor-to-IN/PGND connection is in place, and U16 already uses 0805 capacitors.
where: Frontend FPGA Board, L1. U2 (VCCINT), U3 (VCCAUX), U4 (VCCO_1V5), U13 (1V4_GTP_IN) with input capacitors C1, C12, C21, C85 (22 uF 0603, GRM188R60J226). SW pads (Pad5/15) of these modules. U16 (5 V to 3.3 V) with C207 and C206 (0805) for comparison.
evidence: exports/frontend/pads.csv and board.json: capacitor pad centre to IN pin C1 1.81, C12 1.77, C21 1.80, C85 1.81 mm; U16: C207 1.49, C206 2.09 mm. SW nets 'unconnected-(Ux-SW-Pad5/15)': 0 tracks, 0 zones. IN and PGND/AGND joined to the capacitor pads by 0.35-0.45 mm L1 tracks. Each pin 1 and pin 16 has one 0.1 mm L1-L2 GND microvia; each capacitor GND pad adds two (three at C207). exports/frontend/zones.csv: L2 GND 464 mm2 in one piece, 0.071 mm below L1. exports/frontend/parts.csv: C1/C12/C21/C85 C_0603 GRM188R60J226; C206/C207 C_0805 GRM21BR61A226.
source: MPS MPM3833C datasheet Rev 1.0 (12/3/2018), p16, PCB Layout Guidelines items 1-4 and Figure 3; p3 note 4 (the 42 C/W theta-JA is for the two-layer EVM3833C-RH-00A evaluation board only). https://www.monolithicpower.com/en/products/power-modules/ultra-thin-profile/mpm3833c.html
consequence: More input ripple on VIN_3V3 and less thermal margin than the datasheet figures suggest. At the expected sub-amp loads the risk is small.
suggested_action: Where the space allows, change C1/C12/C21/C85 to the 0805 22 uF part already used at U16 and add a short SW copper patch. Check module temperature and input ripple at first power-up.

title: Two V3 pre-order footprint fixes exist only on the board and would be undone by a library update.
what: KiCad keeps a copy of each footprint inside the board file, separate from the project library. Two of the V3 fixes were made only in the board copies: top paste on the four J3 shield slots, and a 0 mm solder-mask margin on U8. Running 'update footprints from library' would remove the J3 shield paste and silently bring back the 0.10 mm mask web (the thin strip of mask between pads) at U8. KiCad warns about the J3 mismatch but not about U8.
where: Frontend FPGA Board J3 (four SH pads) and U8 (16 pads). Library files LearningFPGA.pretty/Molex_MicroHDMI_46765_1xxx.kicad_mod and LearningFPGA.pretty/TI_RSV_UQFN16_1.8x2.6mm_P0.4mm.kicad_mod.
evidence: Board J3 SH pads: layers *.Cu *.Mask F.Paste; library (lines 289-330): *.Cu *.Mask only. Board U8: solder_mask_margin 0 on all 16 pads; library: 0.05 mm on all 16. 0.4 mm pitch - 0.2 mm pad - 2 x 0.05 mm = 0.10 mm web. exports/frontend/drc.json: 35 lib_footprint_mismatch warnings, J3 listed, U8 not. inputs/frontend/V3_record/START_HERE.md lines 7 and 111 list these as two of the three V3 fixes.
source: Engineering judgement; inputs/frontend/V3_record/START_HERE.md (the three V3 fixes).
consequence: A later revision could bring back two defects the independent check found, with no DRC message for the U8 one. The current order files are not affected.
suggested_action: Copy both fixes into the project library footprints before the next revision, or keep J3 and U8 out of any library update.

title: The J3 footprint was never checked against the 46765-1001 drawing; JLC links the drawing of another variant.
what: J3 is a Molex 46765-1001 Micro-HDMI receptacle with surface-mount signal pins and through-hole shell tabs. Its footprint is KiCad's stock 46765-1xxx pattern, which cites the 46765-1301 drawing; nobody has compared it with the 46765-1001 drawing. JLC/LCSC attach SD-46765-001, which covers only the surface-mount-only 46765-0xxx parts. The 0.25 mm signal pads are a deliberate widening and stay inside Molex's 0.23 +/- 0.03 mm land, so the open points are the slot size and position and whether the tabs suit a 1.574 mm board; only the 46765-1001 sales drawing or a Molex answer can settle them.
where: Frontend FPGA Board J3 (top side, north edge); SH slots at local x +/-3.1, y 0 and -3.36, board (109.4/115.6, 98.28/101.64).
evidence: boards/frontend/LearningFPGA.pretty/Molex_MicroHDMI_46765_1xxx.kicad_mod: descr cites 467651301_sd.pdf; signal pads 0.25 x 0.85 / 0.25 x 1.0; SH slots 0.65 x 1.70 mm drill in 1.5 x 2.55 mm pads, identical to KiCad's stock HDMI_Micro-D_Molex_46765-1xxx (stock signal pads 0.23 mm). Board thickness 1.574 mm; parts.csv MPN 467651001. LCSC C563878 datasheet is byte-identical to SD-46765-001 rev D1, whose part table lists only 46765-0001/0301/0011/0311/0302/0312. Slot pitch 3.36 mm equals the tab pitch in SD-46765-001 sheet 1. The molex.com sales drawing timed out on every attempt.
source: Molex SD-46765-001 rev D1, sheets 1 and 4 (https://www.lcsc.com/datasheet/C563878.pdf); Molex 46765-1001 sales drawing, not retrieved: https://www.molex.com/en-us/products/part-detail/467651001
consequence: If the slots do not match the 46765-1001 tabs, the shell may not seat or may be poorly anchored. The connector is J3's only mechanical retention for the cable.
suggested_action: Get the 46765-1001 sales drawing (or ask Molex) and compare slot size and position and tab length against the 1.574 mm board; adjust the footprint only if they differ.

title: Top-side paste on J3's shield slots supplies about an eighth of the solder the slots hold.
what: The four shell tabs of the Micro-HDMI receptacle go into plated slots through the board and are soldered by pin-in-paste: paste printed on the top pad melts into the slot during reflow. The paste opening equals the pad, which gives roughly 0.17-0.20 mm3 of solder per slot against about 1.60 mm3 of empty barrel. Expect mainly a top fillet, not a filled barrel, on the tabs that take the cable's plugging forces. JLC lists the part as SMD, and the V3 assembly remark asks JLC to make sure all four tabs are soldered but does not ask for hand soldering or a fill.
evidence: inputs/frontend/V3_order/gerber_files/Artix_Frontend_8L_V3-F_Paste.gtp: aperture D31 O 1.500 x 2.550 flashed at the four slot centres, 3.34 mm2 each. Paste 3.34 mm2 x 0.10-0.12 mm = 0.33-0.40 mm3, about half solder by volume = 0.17-0.20 mm3. Slot 0.65 x 1.05 + pi x 0.325^2 = 1.014 mm2 x 1.574 mm = 1.60 mm3 before the tab. Board: F.Paste on, B.Paste off, paste margin 0. V3_review/parts_status.csv and JLC part page C563878: package SMD. V3_order/JLC_ORDER_NOTES.txt line 19: assembly remark. Tab size unknown (Molex drawing not retrieved).
source: Molex 46765-1001 (SMT with through-hole shell tabs), https://www.molex.com/en-us/products/series-chart/46765; IPC-A-610 barrel-fill criteria (engineering judgement).
consequence: Weak shell-tab joints let plugging forces load the 0.4 mm-pitch signal joints. The receptacle can loosen or tear off.
suggested_action: Ask JLC to hand-solder the four shell tabs after reflow, or enlarge the top paste aperture (overprint) once the tab size is checked against the Molex drawing.

title: About 223 vias sit 0.15-0.20 mm from other-net copper, below JLC's general 0.20 mm hole-to-copper figure.
what: The smallest gap from a drilled hole's edge to copper of another net is 0.175 mm, between neighbouring buried vias on L4. About 223 to 226 vias, depending on how a hole is counted, fall between 0.15 and 0.20 mm; none are below 0.15 mm, and the nearest copper is always a via land or track, never a pour. This meets JLC's HDI figures (0.15 mm) but not the 0.20 mm figures in JLC's general rigid-board table. JLC has to say which figure applies to this HDI order.
where: Frontend FPGA Board, mainly inner layers. Examples on L4: buried vias GND (115.82, 109.40), VCCO_1V5 (115.42, 109.40), FPGA_QSPI_CCLK (115.02, 109.40); FPGA_INIT_B / PG_GTP_1V4 at x 106.02; /ASIC8_DATA5 / GND at x 119.02.

title: J3's shell tabs reach only 0.40-0.70 mm into the 1.57 mm slots, and bottom rework sits 0.137 mm from VIN_3V3.
what: Molex draws the 46765-1001 shell tabs 0.55 +/- 0.15 mm long below the body, so on the 1.574 mm board each tab tip stops 0.87-1.17 mm above the bottom surface. With top paste only, each tab is held by a top fillet and a shallow partial fill of the plated slot. Neither the drawing nor the product specification states a board thickness, so Molex has not said this joint can carry cable loads on a 1.57 mm board. A bottom-side touch-up can wick solder up the barrel to the tab, but it is awkward: the barrel is tied to GND on seven layers, needs about 1 mm3 more solder, and the bottom ring is 0.137 mm from C83 (VIN_3V3) and 0.18 mm from R27 (VCCAUX_1V8).
where: Frontend FPGA Board J3 SH slots at (109.4, 98.28), (109.4, 101.64), (115.6, 98.28), (115.6, 101.64); bottom layer L14 rings next to C83 pad 1 (VIN_3V3, 0201) and R27 pad 1 (VCCAUX_1V8, 0201).

Solder 3.34 mm2 x 0.10-0.12 mm x 0.5 = 0.17-0.20 mm3 vs barrel 1.014 mm2 x 1.574 mm = 1.60 mm3. Board J3 SH pads: *.Cu *.Mask F.Paste, zone connections In1/In6/In8/In10/In12. Gerbers: F_Paste D31 at all four slots; no B_Paste aperture; B_Mask 1.5 x 2.543 openings. L14 gaps from the slot rings: C83.1 VIN_3V3 0.137, R27.1 VCCAUX_1V8 0.180, C83.2 GND 0.191, C103.1/.2 0.280 mm. inputs/frontend/V3_order/JLC_ORDER_NOTES.txt line 19: 'please make sure all four are soldered'.

suggested_action: Change the order note to ask for top-side solder only on the shell tabs, with no bottom touch-up. Ask Molex (or JLC on the first build) to confirm tab retention for 46765-1001 on a 1.57 mm board, and pull-test one assembled board.
