title: At the worst-case low 1.5 V I/O rail, the cable LVDS inputs keep only about 24 mV of DC margin.
what: The cable clock, command and SYNC pairs arrive as LVDS (low-voltage differential signalling) into FPGA banks powered at 1.5 V (VCCO_1V5). The FPGA data sheet recommends that an input never goes higher than VCCO + 0.2 V. With U4 at its worst-case low output and the XEM at its worst-case high common mode (the average of the two wires) and swing, the input high level stays below that limit by only about 24 mV. The limit is still met at these stacked worst cases, typical parts leave about 0.3 V, and short excursions above it do not damage the input, so this is a margin observation to confirm at bring-up.
where: Frontend FPGA Board: U4 (MPM3833C, VCCO_1V5) with divider R7 150k / R8 100k (0.1 %); U1 balls P14/R15 (CABLE_CLK) and M14/N14 (CABLE_CMDSYNC) in bank 14, B9/A9 (CABLE_SYNC) in bank 15; LVDS_25 inputs with DIFF_TERM FALSE and external 100 ohm terminations R61/R62/R64 (bottom).
evidence: U4 worst-case low output: 0.591 V x (1 + 150k x 0.999 / (100k x 1.001)) = 1.476 V, so the recommended ceiling is 1.676 V (MPM3833C VFB 591-609 mV; R7/R8 from exports/frontend/parts.csv). XEM worst-case high level: VOCM 1.425 V + 0.454 V / 2 = 1.652 V (DS931 VOCM max 1.425 V, VODIFF max 454 mV). DC margin about 24 mV (25.5 mV if resistor tolerance is ignored). Typical case (VOCM 1.25 V, VCCO 1.50 V): about 0.3 V. Pin standards from inputs/frontend/V2_review_fixes/Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc. The MPM3833C 100 mV p-p load-transient figure (p5) is for a 0-2 A step at 1.2 V output and does not describe this lightly loaded rail.
source: AMD DS181 Artix-7 Data Sheet v1.27.1, Table 2 (VIN recommended max VCCO + 0.20 V); AMD UG471 7 Series SelectIO v1.10, pp.91-93, Table 1-44, https://docs.amd.com/api/khub/documents/IbGcnPFe6eF19RHma_Y~IA/content; MPS MPM3833C Rev 1.0, pp.4-5, https://www.monolithicpower.com/en/documentview/productdocument/index/version/2/document_type/Datasheet/lang/en/sku/MPM3833CGRH-Z/document_id/4426/; Opal Kelly / AMD DS931 LVDS DC table v1.8. DS181 and DS931 were read only through AMD search summaries because the direct pages returned 404.
consequence: Only a unit at the combined low-VCCO, high-common-mode corner would sit near the recommended input limit; no damage is expected. No margin is left for an error in the assumed figures.
suggested_action: At bring-up, measure the XEM LVDS common mode and the single-ended high level at R61/R62/R64 against VCCO_1V5. Trimming U4 higher is possible but also raises the ASIC's 1.5 V I/O supply, so do it only if the measurement and the ASIC limits allow.
already_known: Schematic V46 J3 note ('Unverified: LVDS VIN margin if VCCO_1V5 < 1.45 V'). frontend-power says the margin is smaller than that note implies (minor); frontend-io agrees with a note rating.

title: The only DONE test point is on the bottom between J1 and J2, so it cannot be probed in a mated stack.
what: DONE is the FPGA pin that goes high once the FPGA has loaded its configuration. Its test point TP12 is the only bottom-side test point and sits in the 1.5 mm gap that faces the FPGA-LDO board when J1/J2 are mated; its pull-up R38 is also on the bottom, and the board has no LEDs. Meanwhile TP5 and TP9 both test VCCAUX_1V8, so one top-side pad is spent on a duplicate. This only matters in a mated stack: the Frontend runs from the cable alone, so DONE can be probed with the board unmated, and in the stack JTAG over the cable and INIT_B on TP11 still report configuration status.
where: Frontend FPGA Board: TP12 (FPGA_DONE, U1.F12) on layer 14 at (117.52, 110.20) mm, between J2 (x 104.745) and J1 (x 122.245); R38 bottom at (118.22, 109.95); TP5 (107.72, 102.50) and TP9 (116.85, 121.12), both VCCAUX_1V8, top; TP11 FPGA_INIT_B top.
evidence: exports/frontend/pads.csv: TP12 copper 14; TP1-TP11, TP13, TP14 copper 1; TP5 and TP9 both on VCCAUX_1V8. exports/frontend/parts.csv: J1/J2 bottom; reference prefixes only C, J, L, R, TP, U, Y (no D or LED). Netlist: FPGA_DONE = R38.2, TP12.1, U1.F12 only; JTAG on J3 pins 2/15/17/18. DF40C mated height 1.5 mm from inputs/ldo_a/stack_fit_test_V10/START_HERE.md.
source: Engineering judgement (bring-up access).
consequence: In a mated stack, configuration status can only be read over JTAG or from INIT_B, not from DONE directly. First bring-up unmated is not affected.
suggested_action: Optionally re-assign TP9 (top, south edge) from VCCAUX_1V8 to FPGA_DONE on a later spin; nothing needs to change before ordering.

title: The 1.5 V I/O rail has eleven 0.47 uF capacitors where UG483 lists twelve for its three banks.
what: VCCO is the supply for an FPGA I/O bank. Banks 14, 15 and 34 share the 1.5 V VCCO supply through 20 U1 balls, and AMD's board guide lists four 0.47 uF capacitors per bank, twelve in all. The board has eleven, plus one 1 uF (C61) and two 100 nF (C63, C105) on the same rail, which more than cover the missing capacitance. All other FPGA rail counts meet or exceed the table.
where: Frontend FPGA Board, net VCCO_1V5: 0.47 uF parts C26-C29, C32-C35, C38-C40; C61 (1 uF), C63 and C105 (100 nF), C42 (47 uF). Bank 0 VCCO (E10, R10) is on VCCAUX_1V8.
evidence: exports/frontend/netlist.xml, capacitors between VCCO_1V5 and GND: 47 uF x1 (C42), 22 uF x1, 4.7 uF x8, 0.47 uF x11, 1 uF x1, 100 nF x2; total 47 + 22 + 37.6 + 5.17 + 1 + 0.2 = 112.97 uF. The frontend-power review's count of 12 x 0.47 uF is wrong; 11 is correct. UG483 Table 2-2, CSG325 XC7A35T row, for three banks: 0.47 uF x12, 4.7 uF x6, one 47 uF (note 3). VCCINT_1V0 (100 uF C4 with C89 DNP, 47, 22, 4.7 x3, 0.47 x7) and VCCAUX_1V8 (47 x2, 22, 4.7 x5, 0.47 x8, 220 nF, 100 nF) meet or exceed their rows.
source: AMD UG483 7 Series FPGAs PCB Design Guide v1.14 (21 May 2019), Table 2-2 (Artix-7, CSG325, XC7A35T) and note 3, https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/ug483_7Series_PCB (read from a cached AMD PDF; the URL returned 404 on the check day).
consequence: Small. A PDN (power distribution network) simulation or a bench noise check would show whether it matters.
suggested_action: Record the 1 uF C61 as the substitute and accept it, or add one 0.47 uF near a bank-34 VCCO ball that has no neighbour on a later spin.

title: MGTAVTT power-good is not used, so configuration can start without MGTAVTT being confirmed good.
what: MGTAVTT is the 1.2 V supply for the FPGA transceiver (GTP) terminations. The GTP termination calibration runs only once, during configuration, and needs every transceiver supply valid beforehand. U6 (MGTAVTT) has its power-good pin unconnected and is enabled by the same node that releases the reset supervisor U12, so configuration waits for VCCO_1V5 and MGTAVCC but not for MGTAVTT. It works by timing margin: the supervisor delay is at least ten times U6's soft-start ramp, so only a slow or failed U6 would be missed.
where: Frontend FPGA Board: U6 (TPS74801, MGTAVTT_1V2) pin 3 PG unconnected; U6.5 EN on BOOT_RAILS_PG_3V3 = wired-AND of U4.12 PG (VCCO_1V5) and U5.3 PG (MGTAVCC), also U12.3 MR (TPS389001), R9, TP10; C50 10 nF soft-start on U6.7; C84 1 uF on U12 CT; U12.6 BOOT_RESET_N to U11 (PROGRAM_B / INIT_B) and U14. MGTAVTT_1V2 feeds U1 A2/C1/E1/F3/G2.
evidence: exports/frontend/netlist.xml for all connections. U6 soft-start: 10 nF x 0.8 V / 440 nA = 18 ms (legacy die), or 15 ms at 530 nA (new die). U12 delay: 1.07 s/uF x 1 uF = 1.07 s nominal, about 0.2-0.27 s if the 0402 X6S C84 derates to the 250 nF the record allows. Ramp is inside the DS181 TMGTAVTT limit of 0.2-50 ms.
source: AMD UG482 7 Series FPGAs GTP Transceivers User Guide v1.9 (19 Dec 2016), p.219, https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/ug482_7Series_GTP_Transceivers; TI TPS748 data sheet SBVS074N p.6 (I_SS, VREF, Eq. 2), https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps74801.pdf; TI TPS3890 data sheet SLVSD65A (tPD vs CCT, MR behaviour); AMD DS181 v1.27.1 Table 7.
consequence: A faulty or slow MGTAVTT would give a configured FPGA with badly calibrated GTP termination instead of an FPGA held in reset.
suggested_action: On a later spin, join U6 PG to BOOT_RAILS_PG_3V3 with the existing pull-up; no change is needed for a first build.

title: Bank 14 runs at 1.5 V during configuration while bank 0 runs at 1.8 V, which UG470 says should match.
what: CFGBVS is the FPGA pin that sets the allowed voltage of the configuration banks; tied low, banks 0 and 14 may each run at 1.8 V or 1.5 V, so nothing is overstressed. UG470 still says bank 14 should match bank 0 when it carries configuration pins, and its SPI table lists only matched pairs. Here bank 0 is 1.8 V and bank 14 is 1.5 V, so the flash data and chip-select pins run at 1.5 V while the flash clock runs at 1.8 V; the translator U8 makes the flash side work. Whether Vivado's CONFIG_VOLTAGE setting and design-rule check accept this mix cannot be settled from the files; one Vivado run would settle it.
where: Frontend FPGA Board U1: CFGBVS E12 on GND; M[2:0] = 001 (Master SPI: R12 M0 on VCCAUX_1V8, R11 M1 and F13 M2 on GND); bank 0 VCCO E10/R10 on VCCAUX_1V8 with CCLK E8; bank 14 VCCO on VCCO_1V5 with FCS_B L15, D00 K16, D01 L17 to U8 (SN74AVC4T774) A side (VCCA = VCCO_1V5, VCCB = VCCAUX_1V8).
evidence: exports/frontend/netlist.xml: E10/R10 on VCCAUX_1V8; all 20 other VCCO balls on VCCO_1V5; E12 on GND; mode straps as above. inputs/frontend/V2_review_fixes/Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc: no CONFIG_VOLTAGE or CFGBVS lines. Bank 14 user I/O stays LVCMOS15 after configuration, so the end-of-startup I/O transition issue (UG470 p.87) does not arise.
source: AMD UG470 7 Series FPGAs Configuration User Guide v1.17 (5 Dec 2023), p.9 Design Considerations, Table 2-4 (CFGBVS row), pp.28-29 Configuration Banks Voltage Select, Table 2-6 p.30 (SPI rows), https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/ug470_7Series_Config
consequence: Probably none electrically; possibly a Vivado design-rule warning or error that must be understood and waived on purpose.
suggested_action: Run the XDC through Vivado once (synthesis, implementation and DRC with the intended CONFIG_VOLTAGE and CFGBVS settings) before ordering and record the result.

title: The ASIC's input and output voltage levels are unknown, so the 1.5 V interface cannot be closed.
what: Every ASIC-facing FPGA pin uses LVCMOS15, a 1.5 V logic standard, matching the ASIC's 1.5 V digital supply (DVDD). The FPGA side is known: it reads below 35 % of VCCO as low and above 65 % as high, and drives below 25 % and above 75 %. No document in the workspace gives the ASIC's switching levels, output levels, load, clamp or limits when unpowered, so the files cannot show that each side meets the other's levels. Only the ASIC designer's figures would settle it.
where: Frontend FPGA Board U1 banks 14, 15 and 34 on VCCO_1V5; ASIC lines and control lines on J1/J2.
evidence: inputs/frontend/V2_review_fixes/Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc: 110 single-ended ports LVCMOS15 (including the non-ASIC CLK25_PL, STIM_START_SHARED and EN_GTPWR_1V5) and 6 LVDS_25. exports/frontend/netlist.xml: every U1 VCCO ball other than E10/R10 on VCCO_1V5. inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/ASIC_REFERENCE.md line 175 (U03): ASIC VIH/VIL/VOH/VOL, loading, clamp and powered-off limits absent; lines 34 and 130: DVDD 1.5 V. DS181 Table 8 LVCMOS15: VIL max 35 % VCCO, VIH min 65 % VCCO, VOL max 25 % VCCO, VOH min 75 % VCCO.
source: ASIC_REFERENCE.md U03; AMD DS181 Artix-7 Data Sheet v1.27.1, Table 8, pp.9-10 (LVCMOS15 row).
consequence: If the ASIC pads switch at a different fraction of DVDD, or DVDD and VCCO_1V5 drift apart, there could be data errors or extra current in the ASIC pad ring.
suggested_action: Ask the ASIC designer for VIH/VIL/VOH/VOL at DVDD = 1.5 V and the allowed pin voltage with DVDD off.
already_known: inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/ASIC_REFERENCE.md (U03). Reviewer agrees it is a note.

title: A configured XEM can drive the cable LVDS pairs into the Frontend before its 1.5 V I/O rail is up.
what: The cable clock, command and SYNC pairs use LVDS (low-voltage differential signalling, a pair of wires held near 1.2 V that carry a small current difference) and run straight from J3 to FPGA pins with nothing to disconnect them. The Frontend's 1.5 V supply for that FPGA I/O bank (VCCO_1V5) comes up last, after 5 V, 3.3 V and the core rail, and is off whenever a port's 5 V switch on the HDMI Extension Board is off. In that window the XEM drives about 1.2 V into an unpowered bank, so current flows through the FPGA's input clamp diodes (protection diodes to the supply rail). The FPGA allows up to 10 mA per pin this way even when unpowered, but the XEM driver current and the back-feed into VCCO_1V5 have not been measured or taken from the XEM documentation.
where: Frontend: J3 pins 6/8, 9/11, 12/14 to U1 P14/R15 (CABLE_CLK), M14/N14 (CABLE_CMDSYNC), B9/A9 (CABLE_SYNC); ESD clamps U17/U18; 100 ohm terminators R61, R62, R64. Power chain: U16 (EN = VIN_5V) -> U2 core (EN = VIN_3V3, PG = PG_CORE_1V0) -> U4 (EN = PG_CORE_1V0, OUT = VCCO_1V5). HDMI Extension Board port switches U701-U708.
evidence: exports/frontend/netlist.xml: /CABLE_CLK_P = J3.6, R61.1, U1.P14, U17; /CABLE_CMDSYNC_P = J3.9, R62.1, U1.M14, U17; /CABLE_SYNC_P = J3.12, R64.1, U1.B9, U18. U16 EN = VIN_5V (J3.19); U2 EN = VIN_3V3; U2 PG = PG_CORE_1V0 = U4 EN, U3 EN, U10 EN; U4 OUT = VCCO_1V5. exports/hdmi/netlist.xml: TS3A27518E switches U610-U618 carry only JTAG/VREF nets; U701 is TPS2553DBVR. Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc lines 112-117: LVDS_25, DIFF_TERM FALSE. The J3 note in the V46 schematic lists 'unpowered Frontend' as unverified. DS181 Table 11: LVDS common mode 0.3-1.5 V, typical 1.2 V.
source: AMD DS181 Artix-7 data sheet v1.27.1, Table 2 (p2-3: VIN -0.2 V to VCCO + 0.2 V; 10 mA maximum through the clamp diode in a powered or unpowered bank) and Table 11 (LVDS).
consequence: Clamp current flows into the unpowered bank and may partly power VCCO_1V5. It is probably within the 10 mA limit at LVDS drive levels, but this is not quantified.
suggested_action: In XEM gateware, keep each port's LVDS outputs disabled until that port's 5 V is on and the Frontend link is up; or confirm from the XEM side that each LVDS output stays below 10 mA into a clamp.
already_known: Schematic V46 J3 note (unverified list). Reviewer agrees it is a note.

title: No rule checks skew on the GTP, clock and cable pairs, and the 72 mm ASIC lane skew rule can never fire.
what: Skew is the length difference between the two wires of a pair, or between signals that must arrive together. The custom rule file sets layers for the GTP_Data, Clock_125MHz and LVDS_Cable classes, and width and gap for LVDS_Cable, but no skew or maximum-uncoupled-length limit for any of them. The eight ASIC group skew rules work (at a 1 mm limit KiCad reports 67 violations) but are set to 72 mm, while the longest lane is 15.56 mm, so they can never trip. The pairs match today only because they were drawn that way.
where: Frontend: boards/frontend/Artix_Frontend_8L_V3.kicad_dru (GTP_Data, Clock_125MHz, LVDS_Cable, ASIC1-ASIC8 rules); rule_severities and drc_exclusions in the .kicad_pro.
evidence: .kicad_dru: no skew, length or diff_pair_uncoupled constraint on the pair classes; LVDS rule has track_width 0.08 and diff_pair_gap 0.30; ASIC1-8 rules skew max 72 mm. Scratch DRC copy (kicad-cli 10.0.6) with ASIC skew at 1 mm: 67 skew_out_of_range. KiCad lengths: ASIC1 15.56 mm (13.99 mm of track plus vias), ASIC3 14.76 mm; largest in-group track spread 6.71 mm (ASIC1). Pair lengths: GTP_TX0 P/N 12.38/12.38 mm; refclk 8.55/8.55 mm; CLK 25.25/25.37, CMDSYNC 23.17/23.41, SYNC 6.99/6.95 mm (pad-entry track paths); P/N differ by at most 0.24 mm, about 1.6 ps. drc_exclusions = []. Re-enabling the four ignored checks adds only 4 footprint_filters_mismatch warnings for L1-L4 (bead footprint name vs symbol filter); 0 missing_courtyard.
source: Routing ground rules V1, G07/G08 (numeric skew left TBD); Engineering judgement.
consequence: A later edit could break pair or lane matching without any DRC message.
suggested_action: Before the next edit, add diff-pair skew (for example 0.1 mm) and max-uncoupled-length rules for the three pair classes, and set the ASIC group skew limits to a value that can actually trip.
already_known: codex_overnight_review/CLAUDE_HANDOFF.md V13 (no length, skew or diff-pair rules).

title: Three footprints use generic land patterns that differ from the vendor examples and narrow some pad gaps.
what: A land pattern is the set of copper pads a part is soldered to. U5/U6 (TPS74801) use KiCad's generic VSON land, which is longer than TI's example and leaves a smaller gap between pads. U17/U18 (TPD4E02B04) use 0.30 mm for all ten lands, where TI uses 0.20 mm for the signal lands and 0.40 mm for the two GND lands, so the signal gaps are narrower and the GND lands smaller than TI's. R44/R63 (Yageo 0201) use KiCad's generic 0201 land, unlike the other 41 0201 resistors on the board; Yageo's own recommended land was not checked. These are assembly-margin issues, not functional ones.
where: Frontend U5, U6 (TPS74801, DRC0010J), U17, U18 (TPD4E02B04, DQA0010A), R44, R63 (RC0201, R_0201_0603Metric).
evidence: exports/frontend/board.json. U5/U6: pads 0.85 x 0.28 mm at +/-1.475 mm, outer edge 1.90 mm, gap 0.22 mm; TI example 0.6 x 0.24 mm at +/-1.40 mm, outer edge 1.70 mm, gap 0.26 mm. U17/U18: ten pads 0.30 x 0.55 mm at 0.5 mm pitch, gap 0.20 mm; TI: eight signal lands 0.20 mm (gap 0.30 mm), GND pins 3 and 8 at 0.40 mm. R44/R63: 0.46 x 0.40 mm, gap 0.18 mm, span 1.10 mm; the other 41 0201 resistors use R_0201_ERA1A_Panasonic_0p30Gap, 0.25 x 0.30 mm, gap 0.30 mm. parts.csv: R44 RC0201FR-07150RL, R63 RC0201FR-07680RL (Yageo). The .kicad_dru has a deliberate 0.18 mm pad rule for R44.
source: TI TPS74801 data sheet SBVS074N, p45 (DRC0010J land example); TI TPD4E02B04 data sheet SLVSD85B, p23-24 (DQA0010A land example). Yageo 0201 land not checked against the data sheet.
consequence: Slightly higher risk of solder bridging or tombstoning (one end of a small part lifting) at assembly; no functional effect.
suggested_action: No action now; switch to the vendor land patterns at the next footprint clean-up.

title: C89 is not fitted but still has paste openings on both pads.
what: C89 is marked DNP (do not populate) and is left out of the JLC parts list and placement file, but the bottom paste stencil still prints solder paste on its two pads. The paste will reflow into a solder bump on each bare pad. That pre-tins the pads for later hand-fitting, though a stray solder ball is possible. Seven filled laser vias sit inside its pads, but the order notes say they are copper-filled and planarised, so they are not a paste problem.
where: Frontend C89 (0805, bottom, VCCINT_1V0/GND), pads at (121.85, 103.04) and (123.75, 103.04).
evidence: parts.csv C89: dnp True, no_pos True. JLC BOM and CPL in inputs/frontend/V3_order have no C89. gerber_files/...-B_Paste.gbp: D20 flashes at both C89 pad centres; board.json C89 pads bpaste True. Vias reaching L14 inside the pads: three in pad 1, four in pad 2. JLC_ORDER_NOTES.txt line 17: C89 not fitted; line 4: laser vias copper-filled and planarised. C89 is the only DNP part; TP1-TP14 have no paste.

title: J3 matches the Molex 46765-1001 drawing, pin-1 side included, so 'footprint not checked' can close.
what: Molex drawing SD-46765-001 rev D1 lists 46765-1001 on sheet 2, and sheet 5 (left) gives the recommended PCB layout for this through-hole-tab version. The J3 footprint matches it: pin 1 on the right with the PCB edge at the bottom, odd row farther from the edge, pitch, stagger, pad lengths, slots, slot pads and keep-out; the 0.25 mm pad width is inside the drawing's 0.23 +/-0.03 mm. The HDMI Extension Board's J610 has the same geometry and pin-1 side with 0.23 mm pads, so the straight-through cable lands the pairs on the intended wires (the P/N swap on pins 3/5 is a separate known item). Sheet 2's note 5 points to sheet 4 (the SMT-shell layout, not this one), and the board edge sits 1.78 mm from the front slot centre instead of 1.70 +/-0.05 mm, so the receptacle overhangs the edge by 0.62 mm instead of 0.70 mm.
where: Frontend J3 (Molex_MicroHDMI_46765_1xxx) at (112.5, 98.28), rotation 180, mouth at the y 96.5 edge; HDMI Extension Board J610-J617 (HDMI_Micro-D_Molex_46765-1xxx).
evidence: Drawing sheet 5 left: pad width 0.23 +/-0.03, lengths 0.85/1.00 +/-0.05, pitch 0.4, stagger 0.2, 6.05/4.75 to the near pad ends, slot 0.65 x 1.70, slot pad 1.50 x 2.55, 6.20, 1.70/5.06 from the edge, keep-out 4.70 x 4.34 MIN. Board J3 instance (extracted from the .kicad_pcb; the library copy differs): pads 0.25 x 0.85 at local y -4.775 and 0.25 x 1.0 at -3.55, slots at (+/-3.1, 0 / -3.36), keep-out x 110.15-114.85, y 96.58-100.92. exports/frontend/pads.csv: J3.1 (110.7, 103.055), J3.19 (114.3, 103.055), J3.2 (110.9, 101.83). board.json edge at y 96.5. exports/hdmi/pads.csv: J610 pads 0.23 wide, odd row x 71.855, even 70.63, pin 1 y 147.1 vs pin 19 y 143.5. J3's Datasheet field holds the Molex product-page URL, not the drawing.
source: Molex SD-46765-001 rev D1, sheet 2 (part table, 46765-1001) and sheet 5 left ('Recommended PCB layout, sheet 2 of 5'); sheet 4 pin table. https://www.lcsc.com/datasheet/C563878.pdf
consequence: None for the land pattern; this rules out a mirrored footprint putting pairs on the DDC/CEC wires and 5 V on HPD. The 0.08 mm edge offset only changes the overhang slightly.

title: Nothing from J3 reaches into the 1.5 mm gap above the FPGA-LDO board.
what: J3's shell tabs end 0.87-1.17 mm inside the 1.574 mm Frontend, and top-side pin-in-paste (solder paste printed over a through-hole) supplies far too little solder to reach the bottom. The only J3 feature on the Frontend underside is the flat GND ring around each slot. Under those rings, Option A and the Option B LDO board have only rail tracks and vias and no part pad within 1.5 mm. So J3 sets no short or seating risk for the 1.5 mm DF40 gap between the boards.
where: Frontend J3 slot rings at (109.4/115.6, 98.28/101.64), mapped onto Option A at x 97.9/104.1, y 137.93/141.29 and onto the Option B LDO board at x 97.9/104.1, y 143.74/147.10.
evidence: Tab 0.70 mm maximum vs 1.574 mm board. Mapping: 180 degree rotation x' = 213.5 - x, y' = 239.57 - y (A) / 245.38 - y (B), from FE J1 (122.245, 112.57) and J2 (104.745, 112.57) onto LDO A J1 (91.255, 127.0) and J2 (108.755, 127.0); pin n lands within 0.185 mm of pin n and 124 of 140 net names match (the rest differ only by the '/' prefix). Under the rings (A): ASIC_VDD_FE track and vias and ASIC_REF_VCM at (97.9, 137.93); EN_ASIC_RAILS at (97.9, 141.29); ASIC_REF_VDD and an AGND via at (104.1, 137.93); a GND via and STIM_NEG_12V at (104.1, 141.29). B is the same, shifted 5.81 mm. No LDO top-side pad within 1.5 mm of any mapped ring on either board.
